pps-number-2.en_title: How to get a PPS Number in Ireland
pps-number-2.en_excerpt: What the PPS Number is, who needs it, which documents to prepare, how to apply, what it costs and how long it takes.
pps-number-2.en_content:
What is the PPS Number?

The PPS Number (Personal Public Service Number) is the most important personal identification number in Ireland. It is a unique number with 7 digits followed by 1 or 2 letters (example: 1234567A). It is used to access public services, work, pay tax, receive social welfare payments and access the health system.

Official links: Official information about the PPS Number

Who needs a PPS Number?

You need a PPS Number if you are going to:

  • Work in Ireland (employed or self-employed)
  • Pay tax (Income Tax, USC, PRSI)
  • Access health services (Medical Card, GP Visit Card)
  • Apply for social welfare payments (Child Benefit, Jobseeker's, etc.)
  • Open a bank account (some banks require it)
  • Buy or rent a property (in some cases)

Official links: Apply for the PPS Number on MyWelfare

What you need to apply

To apply for the PPS Number, you need:

  • Identity document: valid passport (Brazilian or another country)
  • Proof of address in Ireland: an electricity, water or internet bill, rental contract or a letter from a public body
  • Proof that you need the PPS Number: a job offer letter, a letter from the Department of Social Protection, or another document showing why you need it

How to apply

The process is run by the Department of Social Protection (DSP) through MyWelfare. For people over 18, the official service allows you to apply for the PPS Number online; if you cannot use the online system, there is the REG1 form.

  1. Make the application through MyWelfare and follow the Department of Social Protection instructions
  2. Provide proof of identity, address and the reason you need the PPSN
  3. If you cannot use the online service, use the REG1 form
  4. The DSP will inform you of the outcome and next steps

How much does it cost?

The PPS Number is free. There is no fee to apply.

How long does it take?

Processing can take from a few days to a few weeks, depending on application volumes and whether you need an interview. The DSP does not publish a guaranteed fixed turnaround time.

Where to apply

Apply for a PPS Number: gov.ie - Get a PPS Number

Good to know

  • The PPS Number is personal and non-transferable. Never share it with third parties.
  • You can only apply if you need the number for a specific service. You cannot apply “just in case”.
  • If you have had a PPS Number before, use the same number.
  • Keep the card or letter with your PPS Number in a safe place.

Frequently asked questions

Can I work without a PPS Number?

If you have started work and have not received your PPSN yet, talk to your employer and to Revenue about registering the job correctly.

Do I need a visa to apply for a PPS Number?

You need to be legally in Ireland. The PPSN is allocated when there is a valid reason to have the number. The right to work depends on your immigration status.

Does the PPS Number expire?

No. The PPS Number is permanent and does not expire, even if you leave Ireland and come back later.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

medical-card-2.en_title: Medical Card in Ireland: Complete Guide
medical-card-2.en_excerpt: What the Medical Card is, who qualifies, the income limits, what it covers and how to apply through the HSE.
medical-card-2.en_content:
What is the Medical Card?

The Medical Card is a Health Service Executive (HSE) card that can give free access to certain health services. Eligibility normally involves a means test, and there are also specific situations in which a card can be granted on a discretionary basis.

Official links: Apply for a Medical Card or GP Visit Card online

Who is entitled?

To qualify for the Medical Card, you must be ordinarily resident in Ireland (living here and intending to live here for at least one year) and pass the income test. The test looks at the family’s weekly net income (after tax, PRSI and USC).

Income limits and assessment rules

What does the Medical Card cover?

  • Free GP (family doctor) appointments
  • Prescribed medicines at a reduced charge (€2 per item, with a monthly cap of €80 per family)
  • Free public hospital care (including surgery and inpatient stays)
  • Tests and treatment in public hospitals
  • Maternity services
  • Dental, eye and hearing services (in some cases)

How to apply

  1. Download the MC1 form on the HSE website or request it by post
  2. Fill it in with your details and your family’s details
  3. Send the form with the supporting documents (identity, proof of residence, proof of income)
  4. The HSE reviews your application and sends the decision by post

How much does it cost?

There is no fee to apply for the Medical Card. Check the income criteria and the applicable rules on the current HSE page.

Where to apply

Apply for a Medical Card: HSE – Medical Cards

Good to know

  • The Medical Card is free for those who pass the income test
  • If you do not pass the Medical Card test, you may qualify for the GP Visit Card, which covers free GP visits (but not medicines or hospital care)
  • The card must be renewed periodically
  • People with specific medical conditions may qualify even above the income limit (a discretionary medical card)

Frequently asked questions

Can Brazilians get a Medical Card?

Yes, if you are ordinarily resident in Ireland (living here and intending to stay for at least 1 year) and pass the income test. A valid Employment Permit or other valid immigration status helps prove residence.

What is the GP Visit Card?

The GP Visit Card covers free family-doctor (GP) visits, but not medicines, tests or hospital care. The income limits are higher than for the Medical Card.

Do I need a PPS Number to apply?

You will need to provide the PPS Numbers of the people included in the application, plus dates of birth and income and expenses information.

Official sources

gp-registration-2.en_title: How to register with a GP (family doctor) in Ireland
gp-registration-2.en_excerpt: How to find a GP, how to register, what it costs and what to do out of hours or in an emergency.
gp-registration-2.en_content:
What is a GP?

A GP (General Practitioner) is the family doctor in Ireland. It is the first point of contact for any health matter. For non-emergency problems the GP is usually the first place to go, but there are other services. In an emergency you can go straight to an Emergency Department or call 112/999.

Who needs to register with a GP?

There is no general rule saying every resident must register with one specific GP. Having access to a GP is, however, very useful for non-emergency care and ongoing health follow-up.

  • Routine medical appointments
  • Prescriptions
  • Referrals to specialists
  • Medical certificates
  • Vaccinations
  • Screening tests

How to find a GP

  1. Use HSE Find a GP to search for practices in your area
  2. Ask friends, colleagues or neighbours
  3. Check whether the practice is taking new patients (some have a waiting list)
  4. Call the practice and ask about the registration process

How to register

  1. Choose a practice (GP practice) near you
  2. Call or visit the practice to check whether they are taking new patients
  3. Fill in the practice registration form
  4. Bring your PPS Number and identity document
  5. If you have a Medical Card or GP Visit Card, tell the practice

How much does it cost?

The price of a private consultation varies by practice. Do not rely on a single figure as the rule: confirm directly with the GP. If you have a Medical Card or GP Visit Card and the visit is covered by the card, the scheme conditions may allow a free appointment.

Where to find one

Find a GP: HSE – Find a GP

Official links: Find a GP through the official HSE finder

Good to know

  • You need to find a practice taking new patients; availability, registration criteria and distance vary
  • If you have a Medical Card, the GP is free
  • In an emergency, call 112 or 999
  • Outside opening hours, many practices have an out-of-hours service

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a PPS Number to register with a GP?

Yes, a PPS Number is required to register with a GP in Ireland, especially if you want to use the Medical Card or GP Visit Card.

Can I go straight to hospital without a GP?

In an emergency, yes – call 112/999 or go to the Emergency Department. For non-urgent matters you should see a GP first.

Official sources

abrir-conta-bancaria-2.en_title: Opening a Bank Account in Ireland
abrir-conta-bancaria-2.en_excerpt: Why you need an Irish bank account, which documents to bring, how to apply and what it costs.
abrir-conta-bancaria-2.en_content:
What is an Irish bank account?

Having an Irish bank account is essential to receive salary, pay bills, receive social welfare payments and manage your finances. Most employers pay salary by bank transfer.

Who needs a bank account?

A bank account is useful for many people, but it is not a general legal requirement for all residents. Whether you need one depends on your situation and on the services you use.

  • Receiving salary
  • Paying bills (rent, electricity, internet, etc.)
  • Receiving social welfare payments (Child Benefit, etc.)
  • Receiving tax refunds from Revenue
  • Making online purchases and payments

What you need to open an account

  • Identity document: valid passport
  • Proof of address in Ireland: an electricity, water or internet bill, rental contract, or a letter from a public body
  • PPS Number: some banks ask for it, but the required documents vary by institution
  • Proof of income (in some cases): employment contract, recent payslips

How to open an account

  1. Choose a bank (AIB, Bank of Ireland, Permanent TSB, etc.)
  2. Book a branch appointment or start the process online
  3. Bring your documents (identity, proof of address, PPS Number)
  4. Complete the account opening form
  5. The bank reviews your application and activates the account

Official links: Compare and understand bank accounts - CCPC

How much does it cost?

Fees and charges vary between accounts and institutions. Do not treat a fixed €4–€6 range as a current rule: check the bank’s charges and compare the options before opening the account.

Where to open one

The main banks in Ireland include: AIB, Bank of Ireland, Permanent TSB, Revolut (digital bank). The Central Bank of Ireland regulates banks in the country.

Good to know

  • Some banks may require you to already have a job or income in Ireland
  • The Irish IBAN starts with “IE”
  • You may need a PPS Number to open an account – if you do not have one yet, some banks allow you to open with a passport and proof of address
  • Digital banks such as Revolut and N26 can be easier for new arrivals

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a PPS Number to open an account?

Most banks require a PPS Number, but some may allow you to open an account with a passport and proof of address. Check with the bank you choose.

Can I open an account without a job?

Yes, it is possible, but some banks may ask for proof of income or require an opening deposit.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

alugar-casa-2.en_title: Renting a House in Ireland: Complete Guide
alugar-casa-2.en_excerpt: Where to look for a rental, what documents you need, what it costs and your rights as a tenant in Ireland.
alugar-casa-2.en_content:
What is the Irish rental market?

The Irish property market is competitive, especially in Dublin and other large cities. Demand is high and prices are high. It is important to understand the rules and your rights as a tenant.

Who needs to rent?

Almost everyone who has just arrived in Ireland starts by renting. The property purchase market is expensive and requires a credit history.

What you need to rent

  • Identity document: valid passport
  • Proof of income: employment contract, recent payslips (usually 3 months)
  • References: from an employer and/or previous landlords
  • PPS Number: in some cases
  • Deposit: cannot exceed 1 month’s rent; as a rule the landlord also cannot charge more than 1 month of rent in advance
  • First month’s rent in advance

Where to look

  • daft.ie – Ireland’s largest property portal
  • Rent.ie – rental portal
  • MyHome.ie – property portal
  • Local letting agents
  • Brazilian community Facebook groups in Ireland (with caution)

How to rent

  1. Search the property portals and agents
  2. Contact them quickly – good properties are rented within days
  3. Book a viewing
  4. Prepare your documents in advance
  5. If approved, sign the tenancy agreement
  6. Pay the deposit and the first month
  7. The landlord must register the tenancy with the RTB (Residential Tenancies Board)

How much does it cost?

Prices vary widely by location. Rents change quickly and differ greatly by city, property and date. Avoid treating old ranges as current averages: look at recent listings and the RTB information.

Your rights as a tenant

  • The RTB (Residential Tenancies Board) is the body that regulates renting in Ireland
  • The deposit cannot be more than 1 month’s rent; the rule about rent paid in advance is separate
  • The landlord must provide a receipt for the deposit
  • The tenancy must be registered with the RTB within 1 month
  • The landlord must give notice to end the tenancy (between 90 and 152 days depending on how long you have lived there)
  • Since 1 March 2026 there is a national rent control scheme for private tenancies and Student Specific Accommodation, with specific rules and exceptions

Good to know

  • Beware of scams – never pay a deposit before viewing the property
  • Check that the property has an Eircode (postcode)
  • Read the contract carefully before signing
  • Keep all payment receipts
  • If you have problems with the landlord, contact the RTB

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a PPS Number to rent?

Not always, but many landlords ask for it. Having a PPS Number makes the process easier.

What is the RTB?

The RTB (Residential Tenancies Board) is the official body that regulates residential renting in Ireland. It registers tenancies, resolves disputes and provides information about tenant and landlord rights.

How much deposit can I pay?

The landlord cannot ask for a deposit above 1 month’s rent and, as a rule, cannot ask for more than 1 month of rent in advance.

Official links: Check renting rules and rights - RTB

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

Last checked: 3 September 2026

comprar-carro-2.en_title: Buying a Car in Ireland: Complete Guide
comprar-carro-2.en_excerpt: How to buy a car in Ireland: what you need, the buying steps, the NCT, Motor Tax and insurance.
comprar-carro-2.en_content:
What do you need to buy a car in Ireland?

Buying a car in Ireland involves several steps: choosing the vehicle, checking its history, transferring ownership, paying the motor tax and getting insurance. This guide explains the process.

Who can buy a car?

Anyone aged 18 or over with a valid driving licence can buy a car in Ireland. You do not need to be an Irish citizen.

What you need

  • A valid driving licence (Irish or foreign)
  • Identity document
  • Proof of address
  • Car insurance (compulsory in Ireland)
  • Motor Tax (the annual vehicle tax)

How to buy

  1. Set your budget (including insurance, tax and maintenance)
  2. Search on sites such as DoneDeal and CarsIreland, or at dealerships
  3. Check the vehicle history (mileage, accidents, etc.)
  4. Take a test drive
  5. Check that the car has a valid NCT (roadworthiness test)
  6. Complete the change of ownership
  7. Pay the Motor Tax and take out insurance

Official links: Official information on VRT - Revenue

What is the NCT?

The NCT (National Car Test) is the compulsory roadworthiness test for cars over 4 years old. A car must pass the NCT to be driven legally. The inspection checks brakes, tyres, lights, emissions, etc.

What is Motor Tax?

Motor Tax is the annual tax to keep a vehicle on the road. The amount varies with engine size and CO2 emissions. You can pay online on the motortax.ie website.

Official links: Pay Motor Tax online

Good to know

  • Car insurance is compulsory in Ireland
  • The NCT is compulsory for cars over 4 years old
  • Motor Tax must be paid every year
  • Check that the car has no pending fines or motor tax debt
  • Consider the cost of insurance - it can be high for new arrivals with no Irish driving history

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an Irish licence to buy a car?

Not necessarily. You can buy a car with a valid foreign licence, but you need insurance and motor tax. To drive for more than 1 year in Ireland you must exchange your licence for an Irish one.

What is the Eircode?

The Eircode is the Irish postcode (7 characters, e.g. D01 F5P2). Every address in Ireland has a unique Eircode. You can look up the Eircode for an address on eircode.ie.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

carteira-motorista-brasileiros.en_title: Driving Licence in Ireland: How to Exchange Your CNH
carteira-motorista-brasileiros.en_excerpt: How Brazilians exchange their Brazilian driving licence for an Irish one through the NDLS, and what it requires.
carteira-motorista-brasileiros.en_content:
What is the Irish driving licence?

The Irish driving licence is issued by the NDLS (National Driver Licence Service). Brazilians can drive in Ireland with their Brazilian licence for up to 12 months after arriving in the country. After that period you must exchange it for an Irish licence.

Official links: Exchange a foreign licence through the NDLS

Who needs to exchange their licence?

Brazilians who intend to live in Ireland for more than 12 months need to exchange their Brazilian licence for the Irish one. The exchange is possible because Brazil has a reciprocity agreement with Ireland.

What you need to exchange it

  • Valid Brazilian licence (it must not be suspended or revoked)
  • Valid passport
  • Proof of address in Ireland (less than 6 months old)
  • PPS Number
  • Proof of residence in Ireland (at least 185 days in the year)
  • Certified translation of your licence into English (if required)

How to exchange it

  1. Complete the online form on the NDLS website
  2. Book a visit to your nearest NDLS centre
  3. Bring your original documents
  4. Pay the fee
  5. Once the application is processed, the licence is sent according to the NDLS procedure; the timeframe can vary

How much does it cost?

Fees and validity periods depend on the licence type and the current NDLS rules. Confirm the amount directly with the official service before you pay.

Where to apply

Apply for a licence exchange: NDLS - National Driver Licence Service

Good to know

  • The rules on driving with a foreign licence depend on your residence status and on the validity of the licence. Check the current NDLS/RSA rules instead of assuming a universal time limit.
  • After 12 months it is mandatory to have an Irish licence
  • If your Brazilian licence expires you cannot renew it in Ireland – you must exchange it for an Irish one
  • Car insurance can be more expensive for holders of a foreign licence
  • If you cannot exchange your licence (for example, because it expired), you will need to do the full process: theory test, lessons and a practical test

Frequently asked questions

Can I drive in Ireland with a Brazilian licence?

Yes, for up to 12 months after you arrive in Ireland. After that you must exchange it for the Irish licence.

Do I need a test to exchange my licence?

No. If your licence is valid and Brazil has an agreement with Ireland, you can exchange it without a theory or practical test.

How long does it take to receive the licence?

Usually 5 to 10 working days after the application, but it can vary.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

impostos-2.en_title: Taxes in Ireland: Complete Guide (Income Tax, USC, PRSI)
impostos-2.en_excerpt: How Income Tax, USC, PRSI and PAYE work in Ireland, what tax credits you get and how to register with Revenue.
impostos-2.en_content:
What is the tax system in Ireland?

The Irish tax system is run by Revenue (Office of the Revenue Commissioners). If you work in Ireland, your tax is deducted automatically from your salary through the PAYE (Pay As You Earn) system.

Who has to pay tax?

All workers in Ireland pay tax. If you are an employee the tax is deducted automatically. If you are self-employed you must file a return and pay your own tax.

Main taxes

  • Income Tax: progressive tax on your income
  • USC (Universal Social Charge): universal social charge
  • PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance): social insurance contribution

How Income Tax works

Income Tax is progressive. For 2026 the rates are:

  • 20% on income up to the standard rate band
  • 40% on income above that limit

The standard rate band depends on your status (single, married, etc.). For a single person the limit is approximately €42,000 per year.

How USC works

USC is a social tax charged on gross income. Rates range from 0.5% to 8% depending on your income. People with annual income below €13,000 do not pay USC.

How PRSI works

PRSI is the contribution to Irish social insurance. The rate is 4% for most workers (with some exceptions). PRSI gives access to benefits such as Jobseeker’s Benefit, Illness Benefit and the old-age pension.

How PAYE works

PAYE (Pay As You Earn) is the system through which your employer automatically deducts Income Tax, USC and PRSI from your salary. You do not need to do anything – the tax is withheld at source.

Tax credits

You are entitled to tax credits that reduce the tax you pay. The main one is the Personal Tax Credit, which for 2026 is approximately €1,875 per year for single people.

How to register with Revenue

  1. Create a Revenue MyAccount account (using your PPS Number)
  2. Register your employment or activity
  3. Check that your tax credits are correct
  4. If you paid too much tax, claim a refund

Official links: Sign in or register for Revenue myAccount · Access Revenue

Where to access it

Access Revenue: Revenue - Office of the Revenue Commissioners

Good to know

  • If you worked for more than one employer you may have paid too much tax and be entitled to a refund
  • The tax year in Ireland runs from January to December
  • If you are self-employed you must file an annual return (Form 11)
  • Revenue can fine people who do not file their tax correctly

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to file an income tax return in Ireland?

If you are an employee (PAYE) the tax is deducted automatically. You may need to file if you have other sources of income, are self-employed, or want to claim a refund.

How do I claim a tax refund?

You can claim a refund through Revenue MyAccount. If you paid too much tax, Revenue refunds it automatically or you can claim it.

What is the PPS Number in a tax context?

The PPS Number is your tax identification in Ireland. It is the equivalent of the Brazilian CPF for tax purposes.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

cidadania-irlandesa-2.en_excerpt: Who can apply for Irish citizenship by naturalisation, the residence requirements, fees and the process.
cidadania-irlandesa-2.en_content:
What is Irish citizenship?

Irish citizenship can be obtained by birth, by descent (Foreign Birth Registration) or by naturalisation. For most Brazilians the route is naturalisation after a period of legal residence in Ireland.

Official links: Apply online for citizenship by naturalisation · Official citizenship and residence guide

Who can apply?

You can apply for citizenship by naturalisation if:

  • You have legal residence in Ireland for a continuous period
  • You intend to continue residing in Ireland
  • You are of good character (no relevant criminal convictions)
  • You intend to remain in Ireland after obtaining citizenship

Residence requirements

The residence requirements for naturalisation are:

  • 1 year of continuous residence immediately before the application
  • Plus 3 years of residence in the previous 8 years (4 years in the last 8 in total)
  • Or 3 years of continuous residence if you are married to an Irish citizen

What you need

  • Valid passport
  • Valid IRP (Irish Residence Permit)
  • Proof of residence in Ireland
  • Birth certificate (translated if necessary)
  • Proof of address
  • Proof of good character (criminal record certificate)

How to apply

  1. Complete the naturalisation form (Form 8)
  2. Gather all required documents
  3. Send the application with the fee to the Department of Justice
  4. Wait for the assessment (it can take several months)
  5. If approved, attend the citizenship ceremony

How much does it cost?

The naturalisation application fee is €175 (not refundable). If approved, the certificate fee is €950 for adults.

How long does it take?

Processing can take from 6 to 12 months or more, depending on application volumes. The Department of Justice does not publish a guaranteed fixed timeframe.

Where to apply

Apply for citizenship: Irish Immigration - How to Become a Citizen

Good to know

  • Ireland allows dual citizenship – you do not have to give up Brazilian citizenship
  • Residence time is counted from your immigration registration (IRP)
  • Student (Stamp 2) residence periods count only in part
  • If you have Irish ancestry (grandparents or great-grandparents) you may be entitled to citizenship by Foreign Birth Registration

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to give up my Brazilian citizenship?

No. Ireland allows dual citizenship, and so does Brazil. You can hold both citizenships.

How much residence is required?

Generally 4 years of legal residence in the last 8 years, including at least 1 continuous year immediately before the application. Specific categories have their own rules.

What is the citizenship ceremony?

It is an official ceremony where you take the oath of fidelity to Ireland and receive your naturalisation certificate. It is a formal and mandatory event.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

passaporte-irlandes-2.en_excerpt: Who can apply for an Irish passport, what you need, the fees and how long it takes.
passaporte-irlandes-2.en_content:
What is the Irish passport?

The Irish passport is issued by the Passport Service (Department of Foreign Affairs) to Irish citizens. It allows travel to many countries without a visa.

Official links: Passport Online - Department of Foreign Affairs

Who can apply?

You can apply for an Irish passport if you are:

  • An Irish citizen by birth
  • An Irish citizen by naturalisation
  • An Irish citizen by Foreign Birth Registration

What you need

  • Naturalisation certificate (if naturalised)
  • Birth certificate (if a citizen by birth)
  • Identity document with photo
  • Digital photo to the required standard
  • Witness to sign the form

How to apply

  1. Go to the Passport Service website
  2. Create an account or sign in
  3. Complete the online form
  4. Upload the digital photo
  5. Pay the fee
  6. Track the application status online

How much does it cost?

Irish passport fees (online application) are:

  • Adult passport (10 years): €75
  • Child passport (5 years): €20
  • Large passport (66 pages): €105

How long does it take?

Online passport processing usually takes 10 to 20 working days for straightforward applications. Postal applications can take longer. The Passport Service publishes current turnaround times on its website.

Where to apply

Apply for a passport: Passport Service - Ireland.ie

Good to know

  • An Irish passport is valid for 10 years for adults
  • You can apply for the passport immediately after receiving your naturalisation certificate
  • The Irish passport allows visa-free travel to many countries, including the United Kingdom and the European Union
  • If you hold both Brazilian and Irish citizenship, you can use the Irish passport to travel around Europe

Frequently asked questions

Can I have both a Brazilian and an Irish passport?

Yes. Ireland and Brazil both allow dual citizenship. You can hold both passports.

How long does it take to receive the passport?

For straightforward online applications it is usually 10 to 20 working days. Check the current turnaround times on the Passport Service website.

Official sources

child-benefit-2.en_title: Child Benefit in Ireland: Complete Guide
child-benefit-2.en_excerpt: What Child Benefit is, who qualifies, how much it pays and how to apply through MyWelfare.
child-benefit-2.en_content:
What is Child Benefit?

Child Benefit is a monthly payment from the Irish government to families with children under 16 (or under 18 if they are in full-time education or have a disability).

Official links: Apply for Child Benefit on MyWelfare · Official information about Child Benefit

Who is entitled?

  • Habitual residents in Ireland (living here and intending to stay for at least 1 year)
  • Families with children under 16
  • Children under 18 if they are in full-time education or have a disability
  • The applicant must have a PPS Number

How much is it?

Child Benefit is €140 per month for each child. Payment is made on the first working day of each month.

How to apply

  1. Sign in to MyWelfare with your MyGovID
  2. Complete the Child Benefit application form
  3. Enter the child’s details (birth certificate)
  4. Submit the application
  5. Track the status on MyWelfare

Where to apply

Apply for Child Benefit: MyWelfare

Good to know

  • Child Benefit is paid monthly on the first working day of the month
  • Payment is made to one parent (usually the mother)
  • If you have children in Brazil, you may qualify for Child Benefit if they live with you in Ireland
  • The payment is not affected by family income

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a visa to receive Child Benefit?

You need to be a habitual resident of Ireland. Having a valid immigration status (such as an Employment Permit) helps prove residence.

Does my child have to live in Ireland?

Yes. Child Benefit is paid for children who reside in Ireland with you.

Official sources

social-welfare-2.en_title: Social Welfare in Ireland: Benefits Guide
social-welfare-2.en_excerpt: The main Irish social welfare payments, who qualifies and how to apply through MyWelfare.
social-welfare-2.en_content:
What is Social Welfare?

Social Welfare is the Irish social security system, run by the Department of Social Protection. It offers a range of payments for workers, families and people in vulnerable situations.

Official links: Explore and start Social Welfare claims on MyWelfare · Official collection of social payments and services

Who can access it?

Social Welfare payments are available to habitual residents of Ireland. Some payments require PRSI contributions, while others are means-tested (allowances).

Main payments

  • Jobseeker’s Benefit: unemployment insurance for those who have paid PRSI
  • Jobseeker’s Allowance: means-tested unemployment assistance
  • Illness Benefit: payment if you cannot work for health reasons
  • Maternity Benefit: paid maternity leave
  • Paternity Benefit: paid paternity leave
  • Child Benefit: monthly payment for families with children
  • State Pension: the state pension
  • Working Family Payment: income top-up for working families

How to apply

  1. Sign in to MyWelfare with your MyGovID
  2. Find the payment you need
  3. Complete the online form
  4. Send the required documents
  5. Track the status on MyWelfare

Where to apply

Apply for payments: MyWelfare

Good to know

  • For PRSI-based payments (such as Jobseeker’s Benefit) you must have contributed for a minimum period
  • For means-tested payments (such as Jobseeker’s Allowance) you must pass a means test
  • A PPS Number is required to apply for any payment
  • You must be a habitual resident of Ireland

Frequently asked questions

Can Brazilians claim Social Welfare?

Yes, if you are a habitual resident of Ireland and meet the requirements for each payment. Having an Employment Permit or another valid immigration status is important.

What is MyGovID?

MyGovID is the Irish government’s authentication system. You need it to access MyWelfare and other online government services.

abrir-empresa-2.en_title: Opening a Company in Ireland: Complete Guide
abrir-empresa-2.en_excerpt: Types of company in Ireland, how to register with the CRO and Revenue, and what it costs.
abrir-empresa-2.en_content:
What do you need to open a company in Ireland?

Opening a company in Ireland is a relatively simple process. Registration is done with the CRO (Companies Registration Office), and you need to register with Revenue for tax purposes.

Who can open a company?

Anyone aged 18 or over can open a company in Ireland, regardless of nationality. Brazilians with a valid immigration status can open companies.

Types of company

  • Sole Trader: you trade in your own name. Simpler, but you are personally liable for the debts.
  • Limited Company: a company separate from you. More protection, but more paperwork.
  • Partnership: two or more partners trading together.

How to open one

  1. Choose the type of company
  2. Register the company with the CRO (for a Limited Company)
  3. Register with Revenue for tax purposes
  4. Get a PPS Number (if you do not have one yet)
  5. Open a business bank account
  6. Appoint an accountant (recommended)

How much does it cost?

Registering a Limited Company with the CRO costs €50 (online registration). Registering as a Sole Trader with Revenue is free.

Where to register

Register a company: CRO - Companies Registration Office

Official links: Register a company on CORE (CRO) · Register a company - official CRO page

Good to know

  • As a Sole Trader you are personally liable for the company’s debts
  • As a Limited Company the company is a separate entity – your personal assets are protected
  • You must file tax returns every year (Form 11 for a Sole Trader, CT1 for a Limited Company)
  • Appoint an accountant to handle the tax obligations
  • Revenue can fine anyone who files tax incorrectly

Frequently asked questions

Can Brazilians open a company in Ireland?

Yes, as long as they have a valid immigration status. Brazilians on Stamp 1 (work) or Stamp 4 (residence) can open companies.

Do I need an entrepreneur visa?

It depends on your immigration status. If you already have Stamp 4 you can open a company. If you are on Stamp 1 you may need a specific permission. Check with the Department of Justice.

visto-irlanda-2.en_title: Visas and Immigration in Ireland: Complete Guide
visto-irlanda-2.en_excerpt: Which permissions (Stamps) exist in Ireland, who needs a visa and how to register with immigration.
visto-irlanda-2.en_content:
What is the Irish immigration system?

The Irish immigration system is run by the Department of Justice and the Irish Immigration Service (ISD). Brazilians do not need a visa to enter Ireland as tourists (up to 90 days), but they do need a permission to work or to reside for longer.

Official links: Official immigration portal

Who needs a visa?

Brazilians do not need a visa to enter Ireland as tourists for up to 90 days. However, to work, study or reside for more than 90 days you need the right permission.

Types of permission (Stamps)

  • Stamp 1: work permission (Employment Permit)
  • Stamp 2: student
  • Stamp 2A: student not entitled to work
  • Stamp 3: visitor/family member (cannot work)
  • Stamp 4: residence (can work without a separate permit)
  • Stamp 5: residence without a time limit
  • Stamp 6: Irish citizen with dual citizenship

How to get work permission

To work in Ireland you generally need an Employment Permit. The process is:

  1. Find a job with an Irish employer
  2. The employer applies for the Employment Permit to the Department of Enterprise
  3. With the permit approved you can enter Ireland
  4. Register at the Immigration Office and receive your IRP (Irish Residence Permit)

What is the IRP?

The IRP (Irish Residence Permit) is the document that proves your legal residence in Ireland. It is a card with your details and your immigration status (Stamp). You must renew it periodically.

How to register with immigration

  1. Book a visit to the Immigration Office (in Dublin) or the Garda National Immigration Bureau (GNIB) (outside Dublin)
  2. Bring your passport, Employment Permit, proof of address and photo
  3. Pay the registration fee
  4. Receive your IRP

How much does it cost?

The immigration registration (IRP) fee is €300 per year.

Where to apply

Immigration information: Irish Immigration Service

Good to know

  • You must register with immigration within 90 days of arriving in Ireland (if you are staying more than 90 days)
  • The IRP must be renewed annually
  • Do not work without the right permission – this can lead to deportation
  • If you lose your job, notify the Department of Justice immediately
  • Stamp 4 allows you to work without a separate permit

Frequently asked questions

Do Brazilians need a visa for Ireland?

Not for tourism (up to 90 days). To work or study you need the right permission (an Employment Permit or a Student visa).

What is Stamp 4?

Stamp 4 is a residence permission that allows you to work without a separate Employment Permit. It is granted in several situations, such as after 2 years on Stamp 1 or for family members of Irish citizens.

How much does the IRP cost?

The IRP registration fee is €300 per year.

Official sources

irp-renewal-2.en_title: IRP Renewal in Ireland: Complete Guide
irp-renewal-2.en_excerpt: Who has to renew the Irish Residence Permit, what you need and how to renew it online.
irp-renewal-2.en_content:
What is the IRP?

The IRP (Irish Residence Permit) is the document that proves your legal residence in Ireland. It is a card with your personal details, photo and immigration status (Stamp). You must renew it annually.

Who needs to renew it?

All non-EEA residents in Ireland with a residence permission need to renew their IRP. Brazilians on Stamp 1, Stamp 2, Stamp 3 or Stamp 4 need to renew.

What you need

  • Valid passport
  • Your current IRP (if you have it)
  • Proof of address in Ireland
  • Proof of status: Employment Permit, school letter, etc.
  • Photo to the required standard

How to renew

  1. Go to the Irish Immigration Service website
  2. Complete the online renewal form
  3. Send the required documents
  4. Pay the €300 fee
  5. Track the application status
  6. Receive your new IRP by post

How much does it cost?

The IRP renewal fee is €300 per year.

Where to renew

Renew your IRP: Irish Immigration - Registration Renewal

Good to know

  • Renew your IRP before it expires
  • If your IRP has expired you may be illegally in Ireland
  • The IRP is personal and non-transferable
  • Keep your IRP in a safe place – it is your residence document
  • If you lose your job, notify the Department of Justice immediately

Frequently asked questions

How long does it take to renew the IRP?

Processing can take from a few weeks to a few months, depending on application volumes. Apply in advance.

What happens if my IRP expires?

You may be illegally in Ireland. Request the renewal as soon as possible and explain your situation to the Department of Justice.

Official links: Renew your IRP online

mygovid.en_title: MyGovID in Ireland: How to Create and Use It
mygovid.en_excerpt: What MyGovID is, which levels exist and how to create a verified account.
mygovid.en_content:
What is MyGovID?

MyGovID is the Irish government’s authentication system. It works like a “single sign-on” that lets you access several public services online with one account. It is essential for MyWelfare, Revenue and other government services.

Official links: Access MyGovID

Who needs MyGovID?

Anyone who needs to access public services online in Ireland, including to:

  • Apply for social welfare payments (MyWelfare)
  • Access Revenue (tax)
  • Apply for a PPS Number
  • Access health services
  • Renew documents

MyGovID levels

  • Basic: basic account with an email and password. It gives access to some services.
  • Verified: verified account with an identity document. It gives access to most services.
  • Mobile: additional verification with the mobile app for more sensitive services.

How to create an account

  1. Go to the MyGovID website
  2. Click “Create Account”
  3. Enter your email and create a password
  4. Verify your email
  5. To verify your identity you will need your PPS Number and an identity document

Where to create it

Create a MyGovID account: MyGovID

Good to know

  • MyGovID is free
  • You need a PPS Number to verify your account
  • Keep your password in a safe place – it is the key to all your public services
  • Never share your password with third parties

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a PPS Number to create MyGovID?

Yes. To verify your account and access most services you need your PPS Number.

Is MyGovID free?

Yes, creating and using MyGovID is free.

Official sources

direitos-trabalhistas.en_title: Employment Rights in Ireland: Complete Guide
direitos-trabalhistas.en_excerpt: Minimum wage, annual leave, working hours, written contracts and where to get help.
direitos-trabalhistas.en_content:
What are employment rights in Ireland?

Employment rights in Ireland are protected by law and administered by the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC). All workers, including Brazilians with work permission, have guaranteed rights.

Who has employment rights?

All workers in Ireland have employment rights regardless of nationality. This includes the minimum wage, annual leave, working hours and protection against discrimination.

Minimum wage

The Irish national minimum wage is €13.50 per hour (from January 2026). Reduced rates apply to under-20s.

Annual leave

  • All workers are entitled to 4 weeks of paid annual leave
  • Leave accrues in proportion to time worked
  • The employer must pay out unused leave at the end of the contract

Working hours

  • The maximum working week is 48 hours (on average)
  • You are entitled to 11 hours of rest between shifts
  • You are entitled to 1 rest day per week
  • Overtime must be paid or time off in lieu

Contract of employment

Your employer must give you a written contract of employment within 5 days of starting work. The contract must include pay, hours, leave and the notice period.

Notice period

The notice period depends on length of service:

  • 1-2 years: 1 week
  • 2-5 years: 2 weeks
  • 5-10 years: 4 weeks
  • 10+ years: 8 weeks

Where to get help

If you have a problem at work, contact the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC):

WRC: workplacerelations.ie

Good to know

  • The minimum wage applies to all workers, including non-nationals
  • You are entitled to detailed payslips
  • It is illegal to discriminate on the basis of nationality, race, gender, etc.
  • If you were unfairly dismissed you can take the case to the WRC

Frequently asked questions

What is the minimum wage in Ireland?

The national minimum wage is €13.50 per hour (from January 2026). Check the current rate on the government website.

How much annual leave am I entitled to?

All workers are entitled to 4 weeks of paid annual leave per year.

What is the WRC?

The WRC (Workplace Relations Commission) is the official body dealing with workplace disputes, inspections and information on employment rights.

Official links: Make a complaint to the WRC

Official sources

transporte-publico.en_title: Public Transport in Ireland: Complete Guide
transporte-publico.en_excerpt: Buses, trains, Luas and DART in Ireland, and how to pay with the Leap Card.
transporte-publico.en_content:
What is public transport in Ireland?

Public transport in Ireland is administered by the National Transport Authority (NTA) and operated by several companies. The system includes buses, trains (DART, Luas, Intercity) and regional services.

Who uses public transport?

Public transport is used by residents and visitors all over Ireland. In Dublin the system is the most complete, with buses, Luas (light rail) and DART (coastal train).

Official links: Check transport fares and services - TFI

Main services

  • Dublin Bus: buses in Dublin
  • Luas: light rail in Dublin
  • DART: coastal train in Dublin
  • Irish Rail: intercity trains
  • Bus Éireann: intercity and rural buses
  • Local Link: rural buses

How to pay

  • Leap Card: rechargeable transport card with reduced fares
  • TFI Go: mobile payment app
  • Cash payment (higher fares)

What is the Leap Card?

The Leap Card is Ireland’s public transport card. You can buy and top it up in stations, participating shops and online. With a Leap Card the fares are cheaper than paying cash.

Where to buy a Leap Card

Buy a Leap Card: Leap Card

Official links: Official information about the Leap Card

Good to know

  • A Leap Card costs €5 (one-off card fee)
  • You can top it up online, at stations or in participating shops
  • Students may get discounts with the Student Leap Card
  • TFI (Transport for Ireland) is the official transport information portal

Frequently asked questions

What is the Leap Card?

It is Ireland’s rechargeable public transport card. It offers reduced fares on buses, trains and the Luas.

Do I need a Leap Card?

It is not compulsory, but fares are cheaper with a Leap Card than paying cash.

Official sources

susi.en_title: SUSI in Ireland: How to Apply for a Grant
susi.en_excerpt: Who can apply for a SUSI student grant in Ireland, the types of grant and how to apply.
susi.en_content:
What is SUSI?

SUSI (Student Universal Support Ireland) is the official body that administers student grants for further-education students in Ireland. The grants help pay fees and living costs.

Official links: Start a SUSI application · Apply for or check a SUSI grant

Who can apply?

To apply for SUSI you need:

  • To be a habitual resident of Ireland (living here for at least 3 of the last 5 years)
  • To be enrolled in an eligible course (usually at third level)
  • To pass the income assessment
  • To have a PPS Number

Types of grant

  • Maintenance Grant: for living costs (rent, food)
  • Fee Grant: to pay tuition fees
  • Field Trip Grant: for study trips

How to apply

  1. Go to the SUSI website
  2. Create an account
  3. Complete the online form
  4. Send the required documents (proof of income, residence, etc.)
  5. Track the application status

Where to apply

Apply for a SUSI grant: SUSI

Good to know

  • The application period is usually April to November for the following academic year
  • The income test considers parental income (if you are dependent) or your own income
  • The income limits vary according to family size
  • You must be a habitual resident – newly arrived Brazilians may not be eligible immediately

Frequently asked questions

Can Brazilians receive a SUSI grant?

Yes, if you are a habitual resident of Ireland (usually 3 of the last 5 years) and meet the income and course requirements.

When should I apply?

The main window is April to November for the following academic year. Apply as early as possible.

Official links: Apply for a SUSI grant

Official sources

servicos-emergencia.en_excerpt: How to reach emergency services in Ireland, what to say and why your Eircode matters.
servicos-emergencia.en_content:
What are emergency services in Ireland?

In Ireland, emergency services are reached on 112 or 999. Both are free and work 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

Who needs to know?

All residents and visitors in Ireland should know how to reach emergency services. For a medical emergency, fire, crime or accident, call 112 or 999.

Emergency numbers

  • 112: European emergency number (works across the EU)
  • 999: Irish emergency number
  • 112/999: Garda (police), ambulance, fire brigade, sea rescue

How to call

  1. Call 112 or 999
  2. Say which service you need (police, ambulance, fire brigade)
  3. Give your location (address or Eircode)
  4. Describe the emergency
  5. Do not hang up until the operator tells you to

Official links: Garda emergency numbers and guidance · HSE guidance on urgent care

What is the Eircode?

The Eircode is the Irish postcode (7 characters, e.g. D01 F5P2). Every address in Ireland has a unique Eircode. In an emergency, giving your Eircode helps services find you quickly.

Good to know

  • Calls to 112/999 are free
  • You can call from any phone, including a mobile with no credit
  • The operator may speak English – have the basics ready
  • If you do not speak English, say the name of your language and ask for an interpreter
  • For non-urgent medical problems, call your GP or the HSE

Frequently asked questions

Which number should I call in an emergency?

Call 112 or 999. Both work and are free.

What is the Eircode?

It is the Irish postcode. Every address has a unique 7-character Eircode. You can look up the Eircode for an address on eircode.ie.

Official sources

nct.en_title: NCT in Ireland: Vehicle Inspection Guide
nct.en_excerpt: What the NCT is, which cars need it, how often and what it costs.
nct.en_content:
What is the NCT?

The NCT (National Car Test) is the compulsory roadworthiness inspection for vehicles in Ireland. It is run by the RSA (Road Safety Authority) and checks the safety and emissions of the vehicle.

Who needs an NCT?

Cars over 4 years old need an NCT. The inspection is compulsory and the vehicle must pass to be driven legally.

Official links: Book or manage an NCT · NCT - official website

When to do it

  • Cars aged 4-9 years: NCT every 2 years
  • Cars aged 10+ years: NCT every year

What is checked

  • Brakes
  • Tyres
  • Lights
  • Emissions
  • Steering
  • Suspension
  • Bodywork

How much does it cost?

The NCT fee is €55 for cars (full inspection). A retest costs €28.

Where to do it

Book an NCT: NCT - National Car Test

Good to know

  • Driving without a valid NCT is illegal and can result in a fine
  • A valid NCT is required to renew the motor tax
  • If the car fails you have a deadline to fix the faults and get a retest
  • The NCT certificate is valid for 1 or 2 years, depending on the age of the car

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an NCT to buy a car?

It is not compulsory to buy, but the car needs a valid NCT to be driven legally. Check that the car has an NCT before you buy.

How much does the NCT cost?

A full inspection costs €55. A retest costs €28.

motor-tax.en_title: Motor Tax in Ireland: How to Pay
motor-tax.en_excerpt: How to pay the Irish motor tax online, what it costs and what you need first.
motor-tax.en_content:
What is Motor Tax?

Motor Tax is the annual road tax on vehicles in Ireland. Every vehicle registered in Ireland must have its motor tax paid to be driven legally.

Official links: Motor Tax Online

Who has to pay?

All owners of vehicles registered in Ireland must pay motor tax every year. The amount depends on the type of vehicle, engine size and CO2 emissions.

How to pay

  1. Go to the motortax.ie website
  2. Enter the vehicle registration number
  3. Check the vehicle details
  4. Choose the period (3, 6 or 12 months)
  5. Pay by credit/debit card
  6. Receive the receipt

How much does it cost?

The motor tax amount depends on the vehicle. For cars it is based on CO2 emissions, so lower-emission cars pay less. Amounts range from roughly €180 to €2,400 per year.

Where to pay

Pay Motor Tax: Motor Tax Online

Good to know

  • Driving without motor tax is illegal and can result in a fine
  • You need a valid NCT to renew the motor tax
  • Motor tax can be paid for 3, 6 or 12 months
  • Paying for 12 months is cheaper than paying for 3 months

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an NCT to pay motor tax?

Yes, for cars over 4 years old you need a valid NCT to renew the motor tax.

How much does motor tax cost?

The amount depends on the vehicle. For cars it is based on CO2 emissions. Check the exact amount on motortax.ie.

eircode.en_title: Eircode in Ireland: What It Is and How to Find It
eircode.en_excerpt: What an Eircode is, who needs one and how to look it up for any Irish address.
eircode.en_content:
What is the Eircode?

The Eircode is the Irish postcode. It is a unique 7-character code (e.g. D01 F5P2) assigned to every address in Ireland. It was introduced in 2015 and is essential for deliveries, emergencies and services.

Who needs an Eircode?

All residents and businesses in Ireland have an Eircode. You need it to:

  • Receive mail and parcels
  • Give your address on public services
  • Emergencies (112/999)
  • Register with services (banks, doctors, etc.)

How to find your Eircode

  1. Go to the eircode.ie website
  2. Type your address in the search box
  3. Find the matching Eircode

Official links: Find an Eircode

Where to find it

Find an Eircode: Eircode

Good to know

  • Every address has a unique Eircode
  • It is free to look up an Eircode
  • Use your Eircode on all correspondence and forms
  • In an emergency, giving your Eircode helps services find you quickly

Frequently asked questions

What is the Eircode?

It is the Irish postcode: a unique 7-character code for each address in Ireland.

How do I find my Eircode?

Go to eircode.ie and search for your address. The Eircode is displayed.

Official sources

hap.en_title: HAP in Ireland: Help Paying Your Rent
hap.en_excerpt: What the Housing Assistance Payment is, who qualifies and how to apply through your local authority.
hap.en_content:
What is HAP?

HAP (Housing Assistance Payment) is an Irish government scheme that helps eligible people pay their rent. HAP is administered by the local authorities.

Official links: Apply for HAP online · Find your local authority for HAP

Who can apply?

HAP is for people who:

  • Are on the social housing waiting list
  • Have a low income
  • Are habitual residents of Ireland
  • Do not have suitable housing

How it works

With HAP, the local authority pays the rent directly to the landlord. The tenant pays a contribution to the council (usually between 15% and 35% of income). The tenant finds the property on the private market.

How to apply

  1. Contact the local authority for your area
  2. Request an assessment for HAP
  3. If approved, find a property on the private market
  4. The council inspects the property and the landlord
  5. The council starts paying the rent to the landlord

Where to apply

HAP information: gov.ie - HAP

Good to know

  • HAP is for people on the social housing waiting list
  • You have to find the property yourself on the private market
  • The local authority pays the rent directly to the landlord
  • You pay a contribution to the council based on your income

Frequently asked questions

Can Brazilians apply for HAP?

Yes, if you are a habitual resident of Ireland and on the social housing waiting list. Having a valid immigration status is important.

How much do I pay with HAP?

You pay a contribution based on your income, usually between 15% and 35% of your weekly income.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

Last checked: 3 September 2026

rtb.en_title: RTB in Ireland: Your Rights as a Tenant
rtb.en_excerpt: What the Residential Tenancies Board does and how to register a dispute.
rtb.en_content:
What is the RTB?

The RTB (Residential Tenancies Board) is the official body that regulates residential renting in Ireland. It registers tenancy agreements, resolves disputes between tenants and landlords, and provides information on rights and responsibilities.

Official links: Check renting rights and rules - RTB

Who needs to know about the RTB?

All tenants and landlords in Ireland. The RTB is essential to protect your rights as a tenant.

Official links: Tenant rights at the RTB

What the RTB does

  • Registers tenancy agreements
  • Resolves disputes between tenants and landlords
  • Provides information on rights and responsibilities
  • Regulates rent increases
  • Holds the deposit (in some cases)

Your rights as a tenant

  • The landlord must register the tenancy with the RTB within 1 month
  • The maximum deposit is 1 month’s rent
  • The landlord must give notice to end the tenancy
  • In Rent Pressure Zones the rent increase is limited
  • The landlord must provide a receipt for the deposit

How to register a dispute

  1. Go to the RTB website
  2. Complete the dispute form
  3. Pay the fee (if applicable)
  4. The RTB reviews the case
  5. Take part in mediation or a hearing

Where to access it

RTB: rtb.ie

Good to know

  • Check that your tenancy is registered with the RTB
  • Keep all payment receipts
  • If the landlord does not return the deposit you can take the case to the RTB
  • The RTB has decision-making power in disputes

Frequently asked questions

What is the RTB?

It is the official body that regulates residential renting in Ireland. It registers tenancies and resolves disputes.

Does my landlord have to register the tenancy?

Yes, the landlord must register the tenancy with the RTB within 1 month of the tenancy starting.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

cao.en_title: CAO in Ireland: How to Apply to University
cao.en_excerpt: What the CAO is, who applies through it, the key dates and the application fee.
cao.en_content:
What is the CAO?

The CAO (Central Applications Office) is the central body that processes admission applications for higher education courses (universities and institutes) in Ireland. It is the system through which you apply for undergraduate courses.

Who needs to use the CAO?

Students who want to enter undergraduate courses at universities and institutes of technology in Ireland. The CAO is used by both Irish and international students.

Official links: Make or access your CAO application · Access My CAO Application

How it works

  1. Create an account on the CAO website
  2. Choose up to 10 courses in order of preference
  3. Pay the application fee
  4. Send the required documents
  5. Wait for offers in August

Key dates

  • 1 February: normal application deadline
  • 1 May: deadline to change preferences
  • August: offers are made

How much does it cost?

The CAO application fee is €45 (for 10 courses) or €30 (for late applications).

Where to apply

Apply through the CAO: CAO - Central Applications Office

Good to know

  • The CAO is used for undergraduate courses
  • For postgraduate study you apply directly to the university
  • International students may have additional requirements (English, grade equivalency)
  • Offers are based on points (Leaving Certificate or equivalent)

Frequently asked questions

Can Brazilians use the CAO?

Yes, international students can apply through the CAO. You will need a grade equivalency and proof of English proficiency.

When should I apply?

The normal deadline is 1 February for the following academic year. Apply as early as possible.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

direitos-consumidor.en_title: Consumer Rights in Ireland: Complete Guide
direitos-consumidor.en_excerpt: Returns, guarantees, online shopping and where to complain about a problem.
direitos-consumidor.en_content:
What are consumer rights in Ireland?

Consumer rights in Ireland are protected by law and enforced by the CCPC (Competition and Consumer Protection Commission). All consumers, including Brazilians, have guaranteed rights.

Official links: Check consumer rights and guidance - CCPC

Who has consumer rights?

All consumers in Ireland, regardless of nationality. If you buy goods or services in Ireland your rights are protected.

Main rights

  • Right of return: you can return faulty goods
  • Guarantee: goods must work as advertised
  • Clear information: prices and terms must be transparent
  • Protection against misleading practices
  • Right of cancellation: online purchases can be cancelled within 14 days

Online shopping

For online purchases you have the right to cancel within 14 days (the cooling-off period). The seller must refund you within 14 days of the cancellation.

Where to get help

If you have a problem with a product or service:

  1. Contact the seller first
  2. If that does not solve it, contact the CCPC
  3. For financial services, contact the FSPO (Financial Services and Pensions Ombudsman)

Where to access it

CCPC: ccpc.ie

Good to know

  • Keep the receipts for all purchases
  • Read the terms and conditions before buying
  • Be wary of too-good-to-be-true offers
  • The CCPC has free information about your rights

Frequently asked questions

Can I return a product bought in Ireland?

Yes, if the product is faulty or does not match the description. For online purchases you have 14 days to cancel.

What is the CCPC?

It is Ireland’s consumer protection commission. It provides information and help with complaints.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

Last checked: 3 September 2026

protecao-dados.en_title: Data Protection in Ireland: Your Rights (GDPR)
protecao-dados.en_excerpt: Your rights under the GDPR in Ireland and how to exercise them.
protecao-dados.en_content:
What is data protection in Ireland?

Data protection in Ireland is regulated by the Data Protection Commission (DPC). Ireland follows the EU GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation), which gives citizens strong rights over their personal data.

Official links: Exercise your data protection rights - DPC

Who is protected?

All residents of Ireland have data protection rights under the GDPR. This includes Brazilians living in Ireland.

Your rights under the GDPR

  • Right of access: see what data a company holds about you
  • Right of rectification: correct inaccurate data
  • Right to erasure: ask for your data to be deleted
  • Right to portability: transfer your data to another company
  • Right to object: object to the processing of your data

How to exercise your rights

  1. Contact the company that holds your data
  2. Make the request in writing
  3. The company must respond within 1 month
  4. If it is not resolved, contact the DPC

Where to access it

DPC: dataprotection.ie

Good to know

  • The GDPR applies to all companies processing your data in the EU
  • Companies must obtain your consent to process your data
  • You can request copies of your data at any time
  • The DPC can fine companies that breach the GDPR

Frequently asked questions

What is the GDPR?

It is the EU General Data Protection Regulation. It gives citizens strong rights over their personal data.

How do I make a data protection complaint?

Contact the company first. If it is not resolved, contact the Data Protection Commission (DPC).

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

garda.en_title: An Garda Síochána in Ireland: Police and Emergencies
garda.en_excerpt: How to contact An Garda Síochána, emergency numbers and what to expect.
garda.en_content:
What is An Garda Síochána?

An Garda Síochána (pronounced “Garda Siokana”) is the national police service of Ireland. It is responsible for public safety, crime prevention and law enforcement.

Official links: An Garda Síochána

Who needs to know about the Garda?

All residents and visitors in Ireland. It is important to know how to contact the Garda in an emergency and how to deal with the police.

Emergency numbers

  • 112 or 999: emergencies (police, ambulance, fire brigade)
  • Garda Confidential Line: 1800 666 111 (for anonymous reports)

How to deal with the Garda

  • In an emergency, call 112 or 999
  • For non-urgent matters, go to your local Garda station
  • If stopped by the Garda, cooperate and present your documents
  • You are entitled to an interpreter if you do not speak English

Official links: Official Garda contacts

Immigration registration

Outside Dublin, immigration registration (IRP) is done at the Garda National Immigration Bureau (GNIB). In Dublin it is done at the Immigration Office.

Where to access it

An Garda Síochána: garda.ie

Good to know

  • The Garda is approachable and generally helpful with information
  • You can ask for a reference number when reporting a crime
  • If you are a victim of crime the Garda can provide support
  • Never offer a bribe to the Garda – it is a serious crime

Frequently asked questions

What is the Garda?

It is the national police service of Ireland. The full name is Garda Síochána, which means “Guardians of the Peace” in Irish.

Which number do I call in an emergency?

Call 112 or 999. Both are free and work 24 hours.

Official sources

This guide is for information only. Rules and procedures can change. Always check the official source before making a decision.

revenue-myaccount.en_title: Revenue MyAccount in Ireland: How to Use It
revenue-myaccount.en_excerpt: How to create a Revenue MyAccount and what you can do with it.
revenue-myaccount.en_content:
What is Revenue MyAccount?

Revenue MyAccount is the online portal of the Revenue (Office of the Revenue Commissioners) for individual taxpayers. It is where you manage your tax, check your tax credits, claim refunds and get tax information.

Official links: Sign in or register for Revenue myAccount · Access Revenue myAccount

Who needs to use it?

All workers in Ireland. If you are employed (PAYE), Revenue MyAccount is essential to:

  • Check your tax credits
  • Claim a tax refund
  • Register new jobs
  • Update your personal details
  • Access your income statements

How to create an account

  1. Go to the Revenue website
  2. Click on “MyAccount”
  3. Register with your PPS Number
  4. Verify your identity
  5. Create your password

What you can do

  • Check and update tax credits
  • Claim a tax refund
  • Register new jobs
  • Declare additional income
  • Access income and tax certificates

Where to access it

Access Revenue MyAccount: Revenue - MyAccount

Good to know

  • Revenue MyAccount is free
  • You need a PPS Number to create an account
  • Check your tax credits regularly
  • If you paid too much tax, claim a refund

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a PPS Number for Revenue?

Yes. The PPS Number is your tax identification in Ireland and is needed to create a Revenue account.

How do I claim a tax refund?

Go to Revenue MyAccount, check your tax credits and claim the refund. Revenue processes it and deposits it into your bank account.

Official sources

primeira-inscricao-irp-irlanda-brasileir.en_title: First IRP Registration in Ireland: Step-by-Step for Brazilians
primeira-inscricao-irp-irlanda-brasileir.en_excerpt: How the first registration of your Irish immigration permission works, which documents to prepare and what it costs.
primeira-inscricao-irp-irlanda-brasileir.en_content:
Meta description: See how the first IRP registration works for Brazilians and other non-EU/EEA citizens, which documents to prepare, what it costs and where to follow the process.

Suggested URL: /guias/primeira-inscricao-irp-irlanda-brasileiros/

Introduction

If you are Brazilian and have come to Ireland to work, study, live or join family for more than 90 days, registering your immigration permission for the first time is one of the most important steps of your arrival. The current process is carried out by the Immigration Service Delivery (ISD).

Official links: Official information for first-time registration

Who this guide is for

Brazilians and other citizens from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who need to register a residence permission in the Republic of Ireland for the first time.

Step by step

  • Check whether you need to register: the ISD states that people from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who come to work, study, live or join family for more than 90 days must register their permission.
  • Create or access your personal account in the ISD Customer Service Portal and use it to book your first appointment.
  • Prepare the documents specific to your Stamp. The official page lists, among others, a valid passport and proof of your current address; additional documents vary by permission.
  • Attend the Registration Office at Burgh Quay, Dublin. Your documents are reviewed, a photo and fingerprints are taken and the permission is registered.
  • Pay the fee where applicable. The standard fee is €300 for many categories, but exemptions exist.
  • After registration, track the issue of your IRP and keep your passport, address and other details updated with the ISD when needed.

Documents and information needed

  • Valid passport, including the biometric page.
  • Proof of your current address in Ireland.
  • Documents proving the basis of your permission, such as an enrolment letter, employment contract or family documents, where applicable.
  • Your appointment details and any additional documents requested by the ISD.

Costs and fees

Booking the first appointment is free. The standard registration fee is €300 for many categories; exemptions exist. The official fee table was updated on 17 July 2026.

Timelines and important dates

Do not leave the registration until the end of the period in which you are allowed to remain legally in the State. Availability of appointments must be checked on the official portal.

Common mistakes and points to note

  • Paying third parties for an appointment: the ISD warns that valid appointments are made through the Customer Service Portal.
  • Assuming every Stamp has the same documentation or fee.
  • Travelling without checking the validity of the IRP and the return rules.

Official sources

  • ISD - first-time registration
  • ISD - documents and fees
  • ISD - Customer Service Portal

Useful links

  • ISD - first-time registration
  • ISD - documents and fees
  • ISD - Customer Service Portal

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to pay to book the appointment?

No. Booking the first appointment has no fee; the registration fee, where applicable, is a separate step.

Is the fee always €300?

No. €300 is the standard fee for many categories, but exemptions exist.

Can I pay someone to get me an appointment?

No. The ISD states that valid appointments are made through the Customer Service Portal and warns about scams.

Are the IRP and the immigration permission the same thing?

Not exactly. The permission sets the conditions of residence; the IRP is the card that proves the registration.

Official links: Book your first IRP registration through the ISD service portal · Official information on first-time IRP registration

Last checked

Important notice

viajar-fora-irlanda-com-irp-brasileiros.en_title: Travelling Outside Ireland with an IRP: What Brazilians Need to Know
viajar-fora-irlanda-com-irp-brasileiros.en_excerpt: When you can return to Ireland without a re-entry visa, and what to do if your IRP is lost or expired.
viajar-fora-irlanda-com-irp-brasileiros.en_content:
Meta description: Understand when the IRP lets you return to Ireland without a re-entry visa, what to do if the card is lost or expired, and what to check before travelling.

Suggested URL: /guias/viajar-fora-irlanda-com-irp-brasileiros/

Introduction

For Brazilians living in Ireland, travelling raises two questions: can I enter the destination, and can I come back to Ireland? The IRP answers only part of it. The destination’s own rules must be checked separately.

Who this guide is for

Brazilians and other non-EU/EEA citizens who already hold a registered residence permission in Ireland and plan to travel internationally.

Step by step

  • Check the validity of your IRP before travelling. For a visa-national who holds a valid IRP, the ISD states that no re-entry visa is needed to return to Ireland.
  • Check the entry rules of the destination country: an Irish IRP does not guarantee entry to another country.
  • Check your passport, your name and any other documents used for the trip.
  • If the IRP is lost, stolen, has not arrived yet or has an important error, check the ISD emergency procedure before travelling.
  • Do not count on being able to request a re-entry visa after you leave: the ISD states that the emergency procedure must be dealt with before travelling.
  • Keep digital copies of your documents and confirm the airline and destination requirements.

Official links: Irish Immigration Service

Documents and information needed

  • Valid passport.
  • Valid IRP, where applicable.
  • Proof of your permission and of the travel, if needed.
  • Documents required by the destination country.

Costs and fees

A normal return with a valid IRP does not require a re-entry visa where the ISD rule applies. Emergency procedures or specific visas may have their own rules.

Timelines and important dates

Do this check before you buy or confirm the trip, especially if your IRP is close to expiring.

Common mistakes and points to note

  • Confusing the right to return to Ireland with the right to enter the destination.
  • Travelling with an expired IRP or without the card when it is required.
  • Assuming that a renewal request automatically replaces the physical card for travel.

Official sources

  • ISD - Travel and Re-Entry Visas
  • ISD - Registration FAQ
  • Department of Foreign Affairs - Travel Advice

Useful links

  • ISD - Travel and Re-Entry Visas
  • ISD - Registration FAQ
  • Department of Foreign Affairs - Travel Advice

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a visa to come back to Ireland?

With a valid IRP, the ISD states that a re-entry visa is not needed to return to Ireland.

Does the IRP let me enter any country?

No. An Irish IRP does not guarantee entry to another country: you must meet that country’s own entry rules.

What if my IRP card was stolen while I am abroad?

Contact the ISD before travelling to find out the emergency procedure that applies.

employment-permit-irlanda-brasileiros.en_title: Employment Permit in Ireland: When a Brazilian Needs One
employment-permit-irlanda-brasileiros.en_excerpt: When Brazilians need an Employment Permit, the difference between Critical Skills and General, and the main steps.
employment-permit-irlanda-brasileiros.en_content:
Meta description: Understand when Brazilians need an Employment Permit to work in Ireland, the differences between the Critical Skills and General Employment Permit, and the main steps.

Suggested URL: /guias/employment-permit-irlanda-brasileiros/

Introduction

A job offer does not automatically mean a Brazilian citizen can start working. For non-EEA nationals the general rule is that an Employment Permit is needed, unless an exemption applies.

Who this guide is for

Brazilians and other workers from outside the EEA who are looking for a job, changing employer, or assessing a work offer in Ireland.

Step by step

  • Confirm your immigration status and whether you are exempt from the Employment Permit requirement.
  • Check the right type: the current system has nine types; the Critical Skills and General Employment Permits are important examples.
  • Check the occupation, remuneration and other current criteria: the lists can change.
  • Collect the offer and the contract. The DETE states that a contract signed by both parties must accompany each application.
  • Use Employment Permits Online to create the account, submit the application and follow the process.
  • When the Labour Market Needs Test applies, confirm the advertising rules before submitting.
  • Plan ahead: the DETE states that the application must be received at least 12 weeks before the proposed start date.

Documents and information needed

  • Signed offer and contract.
  • Employer and worker details.
  • Role, remuneration, occupation and work location.
  • The checklist and documents specific to the permit type.

Costs and fees

Fees depend on the type and duration of the Employment Permit. Check the specific type on the DETE website before submitting.

Timelines and important dates

General rule published by the DETE: apply at least 12 weeks before the start date. Where applicable, the Labour Market Needs Test involves additional advertising requirements.

Common mistakes and points to note

  • Confusing an Employment Permit with a Residence Permission: the DETE is clear that they are not the same.
  • Starting work before confirming the authorisation you need.
  • Using old lists of eligible occupations.
  • Not checking the DETE’s current processing times.

Official sources

  • DETE - Employment Permits
  • DETE - permit types
  • DETE - Critical Skills Occupations List
  • Employment Permits Online

Useful links

  • DETE - Employment Permits
  • DETE - permit types
  • DETE - Critical Skills Occupations List
  • Employment Permits Online

Frequently asked questions

Do Brazilians always need an Employment Permit?

Not in every case. The general rule applies to non-EEA nationals, but there are exemptions and immigration permissions that authorise work.

Are Critical Skills and General the same?

No. They are different categories, with their own criteria and consequences.

Does an Employment Permit give residence automatically?

No. The DETE expressly states that the permit is not a Residence Permission.
