bolo-cocada-molhadinho.en_excerpt: Chef Sonia Campos @grannymadeireland — a wonderfully moist coconut cake that is simple to make.
bolo-cocada-molhadinho.en_content:
Chef Sonia Campos @grannymadeireland

Ingredients:

3 eggs

Vanilla drops (optional)

1 tin of condensed milk (395g)

A pinch of salt

150g grated or desiccated coconut

1 small can of coconut milk (200ml)

1 cup (120g) of cornflour

1 tablespoon (16g) of baking powder

Method:

Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a medium tin with butter and cornflour or flour.

In the blender, put the eggs, the condensed milk, the coconut milk, the vanilla (if using) and the pinch of salt. Blend for about 2 minutes until completely smooth.

Add the grated coconut and the cornflour. Blend again until well combined.

Add the baking powder last and mix gently with a spoon, or blend quickly just to incorporate it.

Pour the batter into the prepared tin. Bake for approximately 35 to 45 minutes, or until golden brown on top. Let it cool a little before cutting. It stays slightly creamy on the inside — that is the perfect texture for a moist coconut cake!

Chef Sonia Campos’s tip — to make it even moister and tastier, mix in: 3 tablespoons of coconut milk and 1 tablespoon of condensed milk.

Pour the glaze over the cake while it is still warm and finish with grated coconut on top.

It is simply irresistible!
bolo-cocada-molhadinho.en_meta_description: A wonderfully moist, simple coconut cake by Chef Sonia Campos: condensed milk, coconut milk and coconut, baked for 35 to 45 minutes.

primavera-o-chamado-silencioso-para-flor.en_title: Spring: The Quiet Call to Bloom with Consciousness
primavera-o-chamado-silencioso-para-flor.en_excerpt: Text: Juliana Gomes, founder of Escola Mulher Sistêmica. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/juliana.mendes.gomes/
primavera-o-chamado-silencioso-para-flor.en_content:
Text: Juliana Gomes

Founder of Escola Mulher Sistêmica

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/juliana.mendes.gomes/

The arrival of spring in the northern hemisphere is not merely a change of season. It is a subtle yet deep invitation for us to cross a state of transition — one of those that are not always visible from the outside, but that intensely move our inner world.

After winter’s withdrawal, life begins to lift itself again. The light returns, the days expand, nature awakens. And along with it, something in us also shifts. Spring calls us to blossoming, to the beginning of new cycles, to the opening of what was previously gestating.

But to blossom is not only to begin.

To blossom requires presence, support and maturity.

There is a time between the initial impulse and the concrete manifestation of what we wish to live. A time that we often neglect, because we were taught to seek quick results, immediate answers and paths without a crossing.

Spring teaches us the opposite.

It reminds us that everything born needs to be cared for. That what begins needs to be nourished. That the beauty of blossoming lies not only in the result, but in the silent process of growth that happens day after day.

For us, women, that understanding is even more essential. Because life invites us not only to do, but to gestate. To respect our rhythms, our internal times, our capacity to sustain what we choose to live.

And perhaps the greatest challenge of this time is precisely that: not to lose ourselves among the many possibilities that arise, but to remain connected to what truly matters.

Spring is fertile.

But not everything needs to bloom.

Discerning, choosing and sustaining are movements of feminine maturity.

Returning to a consciousness of the cycles is returning to our place.

It is learning to walk with more truth, less urgency and more presence.

Spring has arrived.

And with it, the opportunity to bloom — not out of impulse, but out of consciousness.

At Escola Mulher Sistêmica, we look at life from this perspective: that we are part of a larger cycle, and that when we disconnect from it, we also lose our sense of direction.

Our School is here, close to you, in County Laois, as a living space of reconnection, maturity and belonging to the cycle of life.
primavera-o-chamado-silencioso-para-flor.en_meta_description: Spring is fertile, but not everything needs to bloom. Discerning, choosing and sustaining are movements of feminine maturity.

primavera-chegou-um-convite-para-renovar.en_title: 🌿 Spring Has Arrived: An Invitation to Refresh Your Eating Too
primavera-chegou-um-convite-para-renovar.en_content:
Text: Nutri Marcela

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/marcela.holisticnutrition/

Spring has arrived, and with it the days get longer… The daffodils (those lovely yellow flowers) start appearing everywhere, and a new energy of renewal after winter begins to emerge here in Ireland.

And together with that energy, this is also a great moment to look at our eating with more care. To think about how spring can be a great ally for a lighter, more nutritious and balanced diet.

When we talk about healthy eating, following the seasons makes all the difference. Seasonal foods also count for a lot in that process. So, when you come across produce such as Irish carrots or Irish spinach, choose those options, because they tend to be fresher, tastier and also better for our planet.

And today I want to show you how, with small steps, we can make the most of this season to make our eating tastier and more nutritious — not only for you, but for your whole family.

💚 A little about me

My name is Marcela Ferreira, I am a nutritionist, I have lived in Ireland for 14 years and I work with a gentle approach to nutrition: based on science and without radicalism.

My focus is to help you build an eating pattern for life, improve your relationship with food and make more conscious choices, whether your goal is to lose weight, look after your health or improve a test result.

Because more than numbers, how you feel matters. And caring for your diet is not only about what you do today, but about what you can keep up over the years, creating a healthy and sustainable eating pattern.

And that is why thinking about how to eat well in each season is also part of that process.

For example, in winter… who really feels like eating salad? Our body naturally asks for warmer, more comforting meals.

But that is a subject for another conversation. Today we will focus on spring 🌸 and on how we can make our eating lighter, more nutritious and aligned with this new season.

🌸 How to adjust your eating in spring, in practice

Spring here in Ireland still arrives with milder temperatures. It is only around May that we start to feel a little warmth, or rather, to put away our heavier coats.

We also do not yet have a great variety of local fruit and vegetables at this stage, and that is fine.

What matters most here is not perfection but a simple principle: the more colours on the plate, the better.

If you do not usually include vegetables in your meals yet, start gradually. Try adding at least one vegetable at lunch and at dinner.

And one important point: frozen vegetables are great allies too. They are just as nutritious as fresh ones. The same goes for frozen fruit.

If you do not like them much, start by choosing the ones you already enjoy. The idea is to gradually bring more colour and variety into your everyday life.

Remember: progress is better than perfection 💚

🥗 Do not forget the legumes

Another important point is including more legumes in your diet.

Our traditional rice and beans, so present in our culture, is an incredible example of nutritious and comforting food, and it can — and should — continue to be part of your routine.

Here in Ireland you will find a wide variety of beans in supermarkets such as Tesco and Dunnes, as well as in the small Brazilian shops.

An important tip is to soak the beans for at least twelve hours and change the water at least once. When you cook them, use fresh water, and if you like, add a few drops of vinegar or bay leaves.

This process helps improve digestion, reduces gas formation and also makes the beans more nutritious.

And pay attention to the accompaniments. Processed meats such as bacon and sausage should be eaten more occasionally, and not every day.

You can also vary with other options such as chickpeas, lentils and even hummus. The ready-made supermarket version can be a good option, or you can make your own.

A practical snack idea is hummus with carrot. Simple, nutritious and many children really like it.

And yes, tinned legumes can be an option too. Choose versions with no added salt or ones preserved in water. Just remember to rinse them well before eating, as that helps reduce excess sodium and can also lessen digestive discomfort such as gas, which some people report.

Variety is fundamental to our health, and it does not have to be perfect every day. Think across the week.

🐟 Include fish in a simple way

Another point that is well worth it in Ireland is making the most of easy access to fish such as salmon.

A simple way to prepare it is to season with salt and olive oil and bake at two hundred degrees for about twenty minutes.

You can serve it with potato, carrot and broccoli. Everything can be prepared practically, even in the same pan, with potato and carrot in the water and the broccoli steamed.

🫒 And do not forget the olive oil

Olive oil is a great ally for health and is very accessible here.

Prefer to buy it in a dark glass bottle and store it in a cupboard, away from the light.

💧 Hydration counts too

And one simple but essential reminder: drink water.

Hydration helps the bowel work, helps energy, helps mood and helps the body stay balanced.

Finally, here is an invitation for you to reflect, with this renewing energy of spring. What could you improve in your eating today, even in small steps?

Remember: progress is always better than perfection.

If you feel you need help organising your eating, looking after your health through nutrition, improving your relationship with food or bringing more balance into your everyday life, I am here to help you.

Online and in-person appointments in Dublin and Kilcock

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/marcela.holisticnutrition/

With care,

Nutri Marcela 💚

escalar-e-necessario-crescer-com-consist.en_title: SCALING IS NECESSARY! Growing with Consistency Is the Next Level of Your Business!
escalar-e-necessario-crescer-com-consist.en_excerpt: By Sonia Campos, MSc in Information Science and Specialist in Business Intelligence. instagram: https://www.instagram.com/soninhafields/
escalar-e-necessario-crescer-com-consist.en_content:
By Sonia Campos, MSc in Information Science and Specialist in Business Intelligence.

instagram: https://www.instagram.com/soninhafields/

In the world of entrepreneurship, there is a clear difference between having a business and building a business that PROSPERS. Many entrepreneurs start with energy, dedication and good ideas, but few truly understand the right moment to scale and, above all, how to do it in a structured and sustainable way.

The truth is that every business has a ripening time. Just as a tree does not bear fruit the day after it is planted, companies also need time to put down roots: validating the product, understanding the audience, adjusting processes and consolidating positioning. Skipping that stage can be expensive. Respecting that time, on the other hand, is what prepares the ground for solid growth.

But there comes a moment when not growing becomes the greatest risk.

Scaling is not just selling more. It is growing with strategy, with predictability and with the structure to sustain that growth. And here an essential point comes in: nobody scales alone.

One of the biggest mistakes an entrepreneur makes is believing they have to cope with everything. They do not, and nor should they. Strategic partnerships, smart hiring and the support of qualified professionals are fundamental to minimising risk and accelerating results. Having someone who has already walked the path beside you can avoid expensive mistakes and shorten the time between where you are and where you want to be.

Besides that, scaling requires clarity of goals. It is not enough to want to grow; you have to define how, how much and in how much time. A well-structured scalability goal guides decisions, directs investment and keeps the focus on what really matters.

And speaking of growth, we cannot ignore the power of digital. PAID TRAFFIC, for example, is today one of the most effective tools for scaling a business with speed and precision. It allows you to reach the right audience, at the right time, with a strategic message. But it is not the only way.

Other ways of scaling include:

* Building authority through content;

* Strategic positioning on social media;

* Process automation;

* Well-structured sales funnels;

* Partnerships and collaborations with other professionals and brands.

Each of these strategies, well applied, helps turn effort into scalable results.

Throughout my career as an entrepreneur, digital marketing teacher, mentor and influencer, I have learned that growing is not about doing more — it is about doing better, with direction and intelligence. I love technology, I believe in the power of education, and my mission is to teach other entrepreneurs to see beyond the operational, to step into a more strategic level of their businesses.

If there is one thing I can say with conviction, it is this: growth is part of the process, but it has to be built.

Respect the time of your business, but do not settle into it. Seek strategy, surround yourself with the right people and have the courage to take the next step.

Because in entrepreneurship, growing is not luck. It is a decision.
escalar-e-necessario-crescer-com-consist.en_meta_description: Scaling is not just selling more — it is growing with strategy, predictability and structure. Nobody scales alone.

atividade-fisica-nao-deve-ser-um-projeto.en_title: Physical Activity Should Not Be a Summer Project — It Should Be a Lifetime Project.
atividade-fisica-nao-deve-ser-um-projeto.en_content:
Text: Ana Paula, Personal Trainer

https://www.instagram.com/fitandstrongwithana/

It is very common to see “12 weeks to lose X kilos” programmes. And along with them come extreme solutions: exhausting workouts every day and severe food restriction. Yes, that may well produce rapid weight loss… but the more important question is: could you keep that lifestyle?

Probably not. Because it is not sustainable.

And here is a truth based on my own experience: I lost 35 kg and have maintained that result for more than 7 years. What many people do not notice is that the habits that made me lose weight are, for the most part, the same ones that help me maintain it today. Of course, I make adjustments according to each stage of life, but the base stays the same.

There is no shortcut. There is consistency.

Another important point: physical activity should not be seen only as a tool to “burn calories”. And above all, cardio alone is not the best strategy for weight loss.

Strength training is fundamental in that process. It helps preserve and increase muscle mass, which improves the metabolism and contributes to more lasting results. Cardio, meanwhile, has an essential role for cardiovascular health, energy and wellbeing, and should not be seen only as a means of losing weight.

If you want to improve something in this process, start by changing your mindset:

instead of chasing quick results, chase habits you can sustain.

Because in the end, what brings results is not what you do for 12 weeks — it is what you can keep for life!

Movement is medicine!

To age with health, autonomy and quality of life, we need to stay strong.
atividade-fisica-nao-deve-ser-um-projeto.en_meta_description: There is no shortcut, only consistency. Why strength training beats cardio alone for lasting results, from Ana Paula.

a-caneta-emagrece-e-o-espirito-corre-atr.en_title: The Weight-Loss Pen... and Does the Spirit Keep Up?
a-caneta-emagrece-e-o-espirito-corre-atr.en_excerpt: Text written by: Aria Milioni, Systemic Therapist. It works fast... but did your heart get the memo?
a-caneta-emagrece-e-o-espirito-corre-atr.en_content:
Text written by: Aria Milioni

Systemic Therapist

“It works fast... but did your heart get the memo?”

In recent months I have heard the same sentence in many sessions:

“Aria, I am thinking about using the pen... they say it works very fast.”

And yes — it does work. But the question almost nobody asks is: what happens to the nervous system, to the emotions and to identity when the body changes too quickly?

I am not speaking against medicine — I speak as someone who closely accompanies what

happens inside people when the body changes before the mind and the heart

are ready.

Because losing weight quickly is not just losing weight. It is going through a transformation that

involves the body, the nervous system and the way you see yourself in the world.

And that deserves respect — not haste.

“Less hunger on the plate... more silence in the emotions?”

Medications such as Mounjaro (tirzepatide) were created to treat type 2 diabetes.

They imitate hormones that reduce appetite, increase satiety and stabilise

blood glucose.

In practice, you eat less — and you lose weight.

But there is something deeper here: hunger is not only in the stomach. It is also in the heart.

Many people eat to relieve anxiety, to compensate for sadness or to fill emotional

emptiness. When food drops away quickly, that emotional route is affected too.

And the nervous system feels it.

“Your nervous system did not get the instruction manual”

When the body starts eating much less, quickly, it enters adaptation.

During use, many people report:

● intense satiety

● reduced pleasure in food

● nausea and fatigue

● mood changes

● a feeling of apathy or “switching off”

This happens because food also regulates emotions.

When that regulation changes too quickly, the nervous system has to find new

forms of balance — and that does not always happen gently.

Some people become anxious. Others irritable. Others feel a silent emptiness.

It is not weakness. It is the body trying to reorganise itself.

“And when the pen leaves the scene... who holds the emotions?”

When use is stopped, the body tries to recover the previous balance.

And that can bring:

● increased hunger

● return of emotional appetite

● weight regain

● a feeling of loss of control

But there is something even deeper: if the weight changed fast but the emotional patterns remained, the body can return to the old behaviour — not out of failure, but out of survival.

The body tries to protect the old identity.

And that can generate shame, guilt, fear of gaining weight again — and even emotional

dependence on the medication.

I have seen people who lost many kilos... but still feel trapped inside themselves.

“New body, old inner story?”

Losing weight quickly changes the body — and changes how the world looks at you.

More attention. More comments. More expectations.

And the heart is not always ready for that.

Some people feel proud. Others are unaccustomed to their own reflection.

Because the body changes fast — but identity needs time.

There is also something delicate: for many people, weight functions as emotional

protection.

Protection against exposure. Against vulnerability. Against old memories.

When the weight drops quickly, that protection can disappear — and old emotions

emerge.

And that needs to be held with care.

“Not every heart is ready to lose weight fast”

Not every emotional story supports rapid change.

Profiles that need more caution include:

● people with a history of compulsive eating

● intense anxiety or emotional instability

● a history of trauma or abuse

● a very critical body relationship

● people who lose weight under external pressure

It is not about forbidding. It is about understanding whether your system is prepared.

“When the body loses weight... the soul needs to update”

From a therapeutic and energetic point of view, losing weight quickly is a change of identity.

The mind needs to update the image it has of itself.

The heart needs to deal with new emotions.

The soul needs to integrate a new way of being.

When that does not happen, misalignment appears.

The body changes — but inside, the feeling stays old.

Because weight is not only fat. It is history. It is memory. It is accumulated emotion.

If you are considering using the pen, perhaps the most important question is not:

“Will this work?”

but rather:

“Do I have support to sustain who I am going to become?”

Accompanying that process with therapeutic and emotional support helps sustain:

● new forms of regulation

● new habits

● the reorganisation of identity

● the integration of the new body image

Not as something mystical — but as conscious care.

“It is not about fear... it is about consciousness”

If you are using, considering using, or have already used — it is not about guilt.

It is about consciousness.

Medicine has its place. But real transformation happens when body,

mind and heart walk together.

Because losing weight is not only about numbers going down on the scale.

It is going through a deep internal process.

And when that is done with support, presence and listening — the result is not only a

lighter body.

It is a lighter life.

And that... yes... is real transformation.

canetas-emagrecedoras-emagrecer-ficou-ma.en_title: Weight-Loss Injections: Losing Weight Became Easier... but What About Health?
canetas-emagrecedoras-emagrecer-ficou-ma.en_content:
Text: Nutri Marcela

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/marcela.holisticnutrition/

A reflection on the physical, nutritional and emotional impacts of using these medications

Today I want to talk about the so-called “weight-loss injections”, a subject that is high on the agenda everywhere… on social media, in consultations and even in conversations among friends and family.

The movement is so strong that in some cases people end up feeling excluded for not using them, as if it were necessary to be part of society, often without thinking, about their own health.

This ends up reinforcing a thinness ideal that is often unattainable, unrealistic and, above all, unsustainable for most people.

💉 What are the “weight-loss injections”?

In fact, that name is not the most accurate. These medications were developed for the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes, with medical indication and proper follow-up.

They work by imitating a hormone naturally produced by our body, called GLP-1, which acts mainly in the intestine, helping to regulate hunger, increase satiety and improve blood glucose control.

And did you know that some of these mechanisms can also be stimulated naturally? Food quality, mindful eating and even the order in which we eat can influence satiety and our body’s response.

👩‍⚕️ Who are these medications indicated for?

These medications, known as GLP-1 analogues, are important and bring real benefits when properly indicated.

According to international guidelines, the indication is generally for people with obesity (BMI ≥ 30) or overweight (BMI ≥ 27) associated with comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes, insulin resistance, hypertension, high cholesterol or cardiovascular disease.

And it is important to be clear: I am not against the use of these medications. On the contrary, they represent an important advance in health and can bring more quality of life to people who genuinely need them.

But one reflection remains: is everyone who is using them actually indicated?

⚠️ Points of attention in use

We live in an intense search for quick results, especially when we talk about aesthetics. And in that context it is essential to look beyond the weight on the scale.

Mental health, for instance, deserves attention. The relationship with the body, with food and with one’s own image can be deeply affected.

Another warning sign is the inappropriate use of these medications, without medical follow-up, obtained inappropriately or even counterfeit. This represents a real risk to health.

🥗 The role of nutrition in this process

One of the effects of these medications is a reduced appetite, besides possible side effects such as nausea, queasiness and constipation.

But that raises an important question: how do you guarantee nutritionally adequate eating if you are eating much less?

Without proper guidance, intake can become insufficient in important nutrients such as protein, vitamins and minerals.

And then consequences begin to appear, such as hair loss, fatigue, nutritional deficiencies and a worse quality of life.

Besides that, reduced eating can lead to loss of lean mass, that is, loss of muscle, which directly impacts metabolism and long-term health. This process can increase the risk of sarcopenia and also contribute to more pronounced weight regain in the future.

🧠 Hunger, behaviour and “food noise”

Many people report that with the medication, the so-called “food noise”, or food noise, decreases.

But it is important to remember that hunger is an important physiological signal from our body. We should not be afraid of it. The goal is not to eliminate hunger, but to learn to understand and regulate it.

And more: these medications do not directly treat emotional hunger. If there is no work on eating behaviour, those patterns tend to return when use is stopped.

🔄 What happens afterwards?

One point that needs considering is what happens after the weight loss.

The body, naturally, tends to reduce the metabolism as an adaptation mechanism. In other words, maintaining the lost weight may become a bigger challenge.

Besides that, when there is significant loss of muscle mass, the risk of weight regain increases even further.

And that leads us to an important reflection: if we are talking about medications used for chronic conditions, are we not perhaps facing treatments that may be needed for a lifetime?

💚 A final reflection

In the search for quick solutions, we often forget that health is a process.

Caring for the body involves eating, movement, mental health and behaviour.

There is nothing wrong in wanting to lose weight. But it is important to reflect: is this being done for health, or only for aesthetic pressure?

Being thin is not a synonym for health.

Real transformation happens when we manage to build a more balanced relationship with our body and with food.

As Carl Jung once said:

“That to which you resist, persists. That which you accept, transforms.”

If you are indicated for these medications, talk to your doctor and seek proper follow-up.

Now, if the motivation is purely aesthetic,

it is worth reflecting more carefully. Not everything that seems easy at the beginning is sustainable in the long term.

If you would like to understand better how to look after your eating in a balanced, sustainable and more conscious way, I am here to help you.

Online and in-person appointments in Dublin and Kilcock

@marcela.holisticnutrition

With care,

Nutri Marcela 💚

cupcake-da-granny.en_excerpt: Chef Sonia Campos @grannymadeireland — an economical, soft, moist and super simple cupcake batter the children will love.
cupcake-da-granny.en_content:
Chef Sonia Campos @grannymadeireland

Thinking about the cost of the ingredients, I developed this perfect batter! Economical, soft, moist and super simple to make.

It can be made in a blender or even mixed by hand with a whisk.

The children are going to love it!!!

WRITE DOWN THE RECIPE:

1 large egg (60g), 250g whole milk

1 teacup (115g) of soya or sunflower oil

Half a teacup (240g) of wheat flour

2 teacups (180g) of sugar

1 teacup (30g) of 50% cocoa powder

2 tablespoons (15g) of baking powder

1 tablespoon of cornflour

Tip: TO MAKE THE WHITE BATTER, JUST LEAVE OUT THE COCOA

POWDER AND ADD 15ML OF VANILLA ESSENCE OR

GRATED VANILLA POD.

Blend everything in the blender for 5 min.

Pour into a bowl and gradually add the sifted wheat flour, beat well and last of all

add the baking powder. Bake in a preheated oven at 180 degrees.

TOPPING MADE WITH GOURMET BRIGADEIRO:

1 tin of

condensed milk,

200g of cream,

20g of cocoa powder,

100g of chocolate, milk or dark chocolate,

15g of unsalted butter (it gives the topping extra shine).

Put it on the heat, stirring slowly until it reaches a soft stage. Let it cool and cover your

cupcakes.

Another option, instead of topping, is to fill your cupcakes

with this brigadeiro.

papo-de-empreendedor-com-um-toque-criati.en_title: Entrepreneur Chat: A Creative, Light and Motivating Talk to Inspire Anyone Thinking of Starting a Business — and to Provoke Good Laughs and Deep Reflections 😉
papo-de-empreendedor-com-um-toque-criati.en_excerpt: Cristiane Lima, nail designer, manicure and pedicure, on restarting her business in Ireland — her fears, her lessons and her motto.
papo-de-empreendedor-com-um-toque-criati.en_content:
1. Who are you?

My name is Cristiane Lima, I am a nail designer, manicure and pedicure technician. My journey in the world of nails began in 2015, in Brazil, when I decided to turn my passion for beauty into a profession.

https://www.instagram.com/espacocris.nails/

It was in Brazil that I did my first training in the field and started building my professional experience. From the very beginning, I always saw the world of nails as something much more than aesthetics. For me, every appointment represents self-esteem, care, confidence and a connection with each client.

Over these 10 years I have kept evolving, learning new techniques and understanding more and more the importance of delivering work with excellence, attention to detail and professionalism.

In 2022 I arrived in Portugal and started taking on a few clients, trying to restart my career in a new country. But at that moment I faced insecurities, fear and the natural challenges of starting from zero far from home. I ended up giving up for a while, but my passion for the profession never stopped existing inside me.

Today, living in Ireland, I decided to come back with everything and start again even stronger and more professionally. Here in Ireland I have also done new training to update my techniques, sharpen my knowledge and offer an increasingly qualified service.

And my journey does not stop here: soon I will do another course in Portugal, because I believe a professional of excellence never stops evolving. I want to keep growing, learning and keeping up with new trends and techniques to always deliver the best to my clients.

My goal is to build a body of work that is seen, recognised and admired for its professionalism, its quality and its attention to every detail — not only for my personal growth, but above all to provide a special experience for every woman who sits in my chair.

2. At what moment did you realise you wanted to start a business, and how did you choose this niche?

I realised I wanted to start a business when I understood that I could build something of my own, with my own identity, my quality standard and my way of serving. I chose the beauty niche because I have always liked turning small details into self-esteem.

The world of nails enchanted me because it brings together technique, creativity, care and connection with people. Every appointment is an opportunity to make someone feel more beautiful, more confident and happier.

3. What was your greatest fear or challenge in this process?

My greatest challenge was believing that I could start again in another country. Leaving the comfort zone, facing insecurities and starting over again takes a lot of courage. But I learned that every difficult phase is also part of building our story.

4. What was the biggest mishap of your entrepreneurial journey that you now laugh about? 😂

One of the biggest mishaps was realising that being an entrepreneur is not just about doing beautiful nails. There is a diary, materials, promotion, service, organisation, invoicing and still keeping your emotions balanced. Today I laugh, but at the beginning I almost went mad trying to be the manicurist, the social media manager, the accountant and the receptionist all at once. 😂

5. If you did not have this business, which other niche would you have tried?

Probably something connected to fashion, aesthetics or creative communication. I have always liked everything involving beauty, self-esteem and connection with people.

6. What is your life motto?

“Do everything with love, dedication and excellence, because the details speak for you.”

7. Today, what does success mean to you?

Success, for me, is balance. It is having financial results, professional recognition, freedom and, above all, knowing that my work makes a positive impact on people’s lives.

8. Which small everyday victory gives you that quiet happiness?

When a client looks at the final result and smiles spontaneously. It is a simple detail, but it reminds me every day why I chose this profession.

9. Which habit or change of mindset transformed your business?

Understanding that I needed to value myself professionally. When I started looking at my work more seriously, investing in knowledge and stopping being afraid of charging what my work is worth, everything began to change.

10. What do you think could be improved in your business?

I always believe I can improve my digital presence, my organisation and my clients’ experience. Being an entrepreneur means being in constant evolution.

11. What honest advice would you give to someone who wants to start a business?

Do not romanticise the journey. Being an entrepreneur is wonderful, but it is also tiring, and it demands discipline, consistency and a lot of patience. Not every day will be motivating, but carrying on even on the hard days makes all the difference.
papo-de-empreendedor-com-um-toque-criati.en_meta_description: Cristiane Lima, nail designer, on starting over in Ireland: her greatest fear, her funniest misstep and her honest advice for new entrepreneurs.

a-medicacao-pode-ajudar-a-abrir-a-porta-.en_title: Medication Can Help Open the Door, but Training and Habit Change Are What Will Keep the Results
a-medicacao-pode-ajudar-a-abrir-a-porta-.en_content:
Text: Ana Paula, Personal Trainer

https://www.instagram.com/fitandstrongwithana/

Medication can help open the door, but training and the change of habits are what will keep the results. First I want to say that I do not believe that Mounjaro/Ozempic, or GLP-1 class medication in general, is only a “shortcut” — but I also do not believe it should be used by anyone who simply thinks they need to lose weight!

For some people these medications can change lives, especially those who have been struggling for years with obesity, compulsive eating or insulin resistance.

And science has already shown that the benefits go beyond weight loss. The SELECT study, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, demonstrated that semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy) significantly reduced the risk of cardiovascular events in people with obesity or excess weight, even without diabetes.

But I also have to say this: it is not a magic solution.

I see a lot of people assuming the pen does the whole job. The reality is that these medications can help a great deal with weight loss, BUT without strength training, sufficient protein and a change of habits, there is a risk of losing muscle mass as well, not just fat.

And this is important: recent studies on body composition in GLP-1 users show that part of the weight loss can come from lean mass, which makes strength training even more important during the process.

If you are using Ozempic or Mounjaro — and I hope under medical supervision — strength training becomes even more important.

The goal should not just be to “weigh less”. The goal should be:

✔ lose fat

✔ maintain (or gain) muscle mass

✔ improve metabolic health

✔ build sustainable habits

Another important point: studies show that when the medication is combined with physical exercise, the results tend to be more sustainable and less likely to be regained.

The truth is this:

Medication can help open the door, but training and the change of habits will help keep the results.

As a personal trainer, my opinion is simple: I do not judge those who use it, but I always reinforce the importance of using it with medical accompaniment and genuinely in necessary cases.

Now imagine that, out of nowhere, you decide you want to use it to lose 2kg because you think you need to, and to stop eating compulsively, or to silence the “food noise” as we call it in English?

I do not believe that is the best solution, and when you stop the medication? I believe the best solution and the most efficient way to lose the weight in that case and keep it off would be to work on the reasons why you eat compulsively and on the reasons behind the “food noise”.

To finish, my view is this: these tools can be extremely useful when properly indicated, but what really sustains results in the long term continues to be the basics done well: consistency, training, eating and a change of behaviour.

References:

1. Rubino D. et al. Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity (SURMOUNT-1). New England Journal of Medicine. 2. Lincoff AM. et al. Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes (SELECT). New England Journal of Medicine. 3. Recent reviews on body composition and lean mass loss with GLP-1 therapies (lean mass preservation). PubMed Central. 4. Studies on weight loss maintenance with exercise + GLP-1. The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology.

o-que-todo-pequeno-empreendedor-precisa-.en_title: What Every Small Entrepreneur Needs to Learn to Make the Business Grow. Why understanding every area of the company can be the difference between growing or closing the doors?
o-que-todo-pequeno-empreendedor-precisa-.en_excerpt: Nine areas every small entrepreneur has to wear at the same time — from financial control and pricing to customer service, photos and strategy.
o-que-todo-pequeno-empreendedor-precisa-.en_content:
Hello, my name is Tatiane and this subject really spoke to me when I started Dunamase Hampers, and it matched Cristiane’s Mini Interview (I will leave the link here):

https://tdcriativo.wixsite.com/brasileirosnairlanda/post/papo-de-empreendedor-com-um-toque-criativo-leve-e-motivador-para-inspirar-quem-pensa-em-empreende-13

Being very honest, I loved making gift baskets, but I discovered that I love everything involving this world of entrepreneurship, and so TD Criativo was born, https://www.instagram.com/coachpatriciavidal/ and then the ConexãoBr project https://www.instagram.com/conexaobr.ie/, which is an arm of our Virtual Magazine (a special mention to Patricia Vidal:) https://www.instagram.com/coachpatriciavidal/

Entrepreneurship is, for many, the fulfilment of a dream. The possibility of turning a skill, a passion or a market need into income makes thousands of people start small businesses every year. However, there is a reality that is rarely shown on social media: at the beginning, the entrepreneur has to learn to perform several roles at the same time.

Before being able to hire specialised professionals or build a team, it is common for the entrepreneur to be the finance person, the salesperson, the person responsible for marketing, purchasing, customer service and even for solving daily problems.

Although challenging, understanding the basics of each area is not only a necessity — it is a survival and growth strategy for the business.

According to Michael Gerber (2001), many small businesses fail because the entrepreneur masters only the technical part of the service or product, but never learns to run the company as a system. In other words, knowing how to do something well does not necessarily mean knowing how to manage a business.

1. Financial Control: Without Numbers, There Is No Management

One of the greatest difficulties small entrepreneurs face is financial management.

Controlling income, expenses, profit, costs and cash flow is essential to the health of the company. Many businesses close not because they do not sell, but because they cannot correctly manage the money that comes in.

According to Dornelas (2022), financial control allows the entrepreneur to make strategic decisions, reduce waste and have the predictability needed to grow.

Cash flow helps answer important questions:

- How much is my business really making?

- Am I charging enough?

- Can I invest at this moment?

- Am I mixing personal money with the company’s?

As Chiavenato (2021) says, “what is not controlled cannot be improved”.

Practical tip:

Even without hiring an accountant at the start, simple spreadsheets or finance apps can help with day-to-day tracking.

2. Pricing: Charging Correctly Is Surviving

One of the most common mistakes among small entrepreneurs is setting prices based on a competitor or on a hunch.

Many charge only so as to “not lose the customer”, without calculating costs, time invested, materials, taxes, travel and profit margin.

According to Kotler and Keller (2019), pricing should take three main factors into account:

Costs

How much it costs to produce or deliver the service.

Perceived value

How much value the customer perceives in what you offer.

Positioning strategy

What image you want your brand to convey to the market.

When the price is miscalculated, the entrepreneur can work very hard and still make no profit.

As Sebrae (2023) highlights, financially sustainable companies need a clear pricing policy.

More information in this article with dear Sonia

https://tdcriativo.wixsite.com/brasileirosnairlanda/post/gest%C3%A3o-financeira-o-alicerce-invis%C3%ADvel-de-todo-neg%C3%B3cio-que-prospera

3. Sales Strategy: Whoever Does Not Learn to Sell, Suffers

Selling does not mean insisting on or pressuring people.

In fact, selling means understanding needs and offering solutions.

Daniel Pink (2013) argues that in today’s world we are all sellers in some way — entrepreneurs included.

A good sales strategy involves:

Attracting

Showing your product or service to the right people.

Conversing

Understanding the customer’s pains and needs.

Closing

Presenting solutions and making the buying decision easy.

Companies that invest in the customer relationship tend to sell more and build authority.

4. Invoicing: Professionalism Also Means Knowing How to Charge

Many small entrepreneurs feel embarrassed or uncomfortable charging their clients.

However, charging is part of business management.

According to Robbins and Coulter (2020), organised processes reduce conflict and strengthen the professional image of the business.

Having contracts, defined deadlines, organised messages and clear communication avoids future friction.

Charging is not rudeness.

Charging is respecting your own work.

5. Purchasing and Stock Control

Buying too much can create waste. Buying too little can cost you sales.

Balance is essential.

According to Slack and Brandon-Jones (2022), good stock management reduces operating costs and improves company efficiency.

The entrepreneur needs to learn:

- How much to buy

- When to buy

- Which supplier offers the best value for money

- What really sells

Being organised in this area avoids money sitting still and increases profitability.

6. Marketing and Social Media: Your Company Needs to Be Seen

Today, many companies have social media as their main shop window.

However, posting randomly does not mean doing marketing.

Kotler, Kartajaya and Setiawan (2021) argue that modern marketing involves relationship, positioning and value creation.

Important questions:

- Does my brand convey trust?

- Does my profile show professionalism?

- Am I creating content that answers customer questions?

Companies that position themselves well on social media achieve greater reach, credibility and sales.

7. Photos of the Product or Service: The First Impression Matters

On social media, the image sells.

A good photo conveys quality, organisation and professionalism.

According to Solomon (2020), consumers are highly influenced by visual stimuli during the purchase decision process.

You do not have to start with expensive equipment.

But it is important to invest in:

- Good lighting

- An organised setting

- Sharp images

- Before and after (when applicable)

- Professional visual presentation

Many times, the customer buys with their eyes first.

8. Service and After-sales: Good Customers Come Back

Winning a customer costs more than keeping a satisfied customer.

According to Kotler and Keller (2019), customer retention increases profit and strengthens brand reputation.

After-sales can include:

- A thank-you message

- A request for feedback

- Promotions for existing customers

- Follow-up after the service

Well-served customers not only come back — they recommend you.

And a recommendation is still one of the most powerful forms of marketing.

9. Organisation and Strategy: Growing Without Direction Is Difficult

Companies do not grow on effort alone.

They grow through organisation.

Peter Drucker (2006) said that efficiency is doing things right; strategy is doing the right things.

Having goals, planning and a vision helps the entrepreneur move out of survival mode.

Small consistent actions produce big results over time.

Conclusion

Entrepreneurship requires courage, learning and adaptation.

At the beginning, it is normal to need to take on several roles. That does not mean failure — it means construction.

The good news is that nobody needs to know everything at once.

The secret lies in learning continuously, seeking training and improving one step at a time.

As Peter Drucker once said:

“The best way to predict the future is to create it.”

If you are a small entrepreneur, keep learning. The growth of your business begins with the knowledge you decide to acquire today.

Bibliography

as-relacoes-de-casal-na-nova-era.en_title: Couple Relationships in the New Era
as-relacoes-de-casal-na-nova-era.en_excerpt: When the purpose stops being to survive together and becomes living together with consciousness. Text: Juliana Gomes, founder of Escola Mulher Sistêmica.
as-relacoes-de-casal-na-nova-era.en_content:
When the purpose stops being to survive together and becomes living with consciousness

Text: Juliana Gomes

Founder of Escola Mulher Sistêmica

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/juliana.mendes.gomes/

https://mulhersistemica.my.canva.site/adultecer-para-amar

We are in Valentine’s Week.

A time when shop windows fill with hearts, social media floods with declarations of love and, inevitably, we are invited to reflect on our relationships.

But perhaps the most important question is not whether we are loving or being loved.

Perhaps the question is:

What are couple relationships for in the time we are living through?

This is a question that has accompanied my work with women in recent years. And the more I observe their stories, their challenges and their processes of transformation, the more I see that we are living through a profound change in the way we understand love, partnership and life as a couple.

For thousands of years, relationships had a very clear function: to guarantee the continuity of life.

Our ancestors united in order to survive.

Marriages were, above all, structures supporting the family, the domestic economy, protection and reproduction. Love might exist, but it was not necessarily the centre of the choice.

Survival was.

It was through that model that life reached us.

And it is important to recognise that with respect.

Life went through wars, scarcity, illness, loss, inequality and countless challenges in order to keep existing. Our parents, grandparents and great-grandparents carried weights we can barely imagine.

That is why we also inherit deep beliefs about relationships.

The idea that love demands sacrifice.

The idea that you have to put up with it.

The idea that individual happiness should be put second in order to preserve the family.

The idea that staying is always better than leaving.

But something is changing.

For the first time in history, millions of people are asking not only how to survive, but how to live.

The search for therapy, self-knowledge, spirituality, personal development and emotional health has never been so intense.

People want to understand who they are.

They want to discover their purposes.

They want to find meaning.

And when individuals change, relationships inevitably change too.

Perhaps that is why we see so many questionings emerge.

Couples who choose not to have children.

Women who decide to postpone motherhood.

New family configurations.

Separations that once seemed unthinkable.

People seeking different ways of building a shared life.

I do not believe we are watching the end of love.

I believe we are watching the end of a relationship model that no longer answers the needs of a new consciousness.

The data reinforces that perception.

Brazil has been recording record numbers of divorces, and a significant share of those separations happen before even ten years of relationship.

But perhaps the question is not why relationships are ending.

Perhaps the question is: what did they come to teach us?

In my experience, couple relationships remain one of the greatest paths of self-knowledge available to a human being.

It is in the meeting with the other that our wounds appear.

It is in the everyday life of living together that our lacks, fears, expectations and unconscious patterns are revealed.

The other becomes a mirror.

And we do not always like what we see reflected.

Perhaps that is why so many women begin their therapeutic processes motivated by relationship pain.

Many arrive seeking to save a relationship.

But end up finding themselves.

They discover that some questions are not about the partner.

They are about them.

About their limits.

About their self-esteem.

About their family history.

About the way they learned to love.

About what they believe they deserve.

And here arises one of the greatest challenges of contemporary relationships.

What happens when one person grows and the other stays where they are?

What happens when a woman begins to broaden her consciousness, look at her pain, revise her beliefs and build a new relationship with herself?

That is a delicate but necessary question.

Because relationships are not made only of love.

They are made of exchanges.

Of shared responsibility.

Of common purpose.

Of a willingness to grow.

No relationship can evolve beyond the level of consciousness of the people who make it up.

Perhaps that is why New Era relationships demand something that was not previously so necessary: deep conversations about purpose.

Not only about children.

Not only about money.

Not only about where to live or which goals to reach.

But about who we are becoming.

About what kind of life we want to build.

About which values we wish to sustain.

About what consciousness we want to cultivate together.

I believe the new purpose of couple relationships is not only to guarantee that life continues.

I believe it is to help life to flourish.

To create spaces where two people can grow, mature, awaken and expand their consciousness without having to abandon themselves in order to stay together.

Perhaps our ancestors united to guarantee the survival of life.

Perhaps our generation is being invited to learn something different.

To learn to live this life with more truth.

More presence.

More freedom.

And more consciousness.

Because, in the end, perhaps the love of the New Era is not about finding someone who completes us.

Perhaps it is about finding someone willing to walk at our side while both of us go on transforming.

dois-fatores-que-fazem-o-seu-negocio-ter.en_title: TWO FACTORS THAT GIVE YOUR BUSINESS CONSISTENCY IN SALES.
dois-fatores-que-fazem-o-seu-negocio-ter.en_excerpt: By Sonia Campos, MSc in Information Science and Specialist in Business Intelligence. instagram: https://www.instagram.com/soninhafields/
dois-fatores-que-fazem-o-seu-negocio-ter.en_content:
By Sonia Campos, MSc in Information Science and Specialist in Business Intelligence.

instagram: https://www.instagram.com/soninhafields/

In an increasingly competitive market, many entrepreneurs believe that the secret to success is simply selling more. However, the sustainability of a business depends on factors far deeper than a simple commercial transaction. Among them, two stand out for their capacity to generate loyalty, referrals and continuous growth: welcoming the customer and the buying experience.

The first contact is decisive. Before even evaluating prices or conditions, the customer evaluates people. Kindness, courtesy, lightness, good humour and genuine attention create an emotional connection that opens the door to trust. Demonstrating command of the product or service conveys safety, but just as important is knowing how to listen. Many entrepreneurs make the mistake of presenting their solutions before understanding the real needs of the customer.

When we ask questions, listen attentively and seek to understand the challenges of the person in front of us, we manage to offer a more appropriate and personalised solution. People like buying from those who convey positive energy, credibility and a genuine interest in helping them.

An excellent service may not generate an immediate sale, but it is a guarantee of a future sale!

The second factor is the buying experience. The relationship with the customer does not end when the sale is completed. On the contrary, that is when loyalty begins to be built. Every detail matters: the communication, the service, the delivery, the follow-up and the way the customer feels throughout the whole journey.

Companies that delight their customers create a lasting memory. Delivering more than was promised does not necessarily mean spending more, but rather adding value through attention, care and excellence in the details. A small gesture can turn a satisfied customer into a true promoter of your brand.

Ultimately, consistent businesses are built by people who understand that selling is not just offering a product or service, but creating relationships and memorable experiences. Customers may forget what they bought, but they hardly ever forget how they were treated.

That, in the end, is what differentiates a simple sale from a sustainable company!

Sonia Campos

Entrepreneur and MSc in Market Intelligence.

quem-voce-se-tornou-longe-de-casa.en_title: Who Have You Become Far from Home?
quem-voce-se-tornou-longe-de-casa.en_excerpt: Text written by: Aria Milioni, Systemic Therapist. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ariaenergyhealing/
quem-voce-se-tornou-longe-de-casa.en_content:
Text written by: Aria Milioni

Systemic Therapist

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ariaenergyhealing/

There is a silent trap in the immigrant experience.

It does not happen at the airport.

It does not happen when you say goodbye to your family.

Nor when you realise you have missed birthdays, weddings or important moments of

those who stayed behind.

It happens little by little.

So slowly that it often goes unnoticed.

Because emigrating does not only mean changing country.

It means inevitably losing part of the system that regulated your emotional life. And that is something few immigrants understand when they arrive.

When we lived close to family, friends or people who knew us

deeply, there was an invisible network supporting our emotional balance.

A spontaneous conversation. A Sunday lunch. An unexpected visit. A hug

without needing to book it in the diary.

All of that helped our nervous system remember that we were safe.

When we emigrate, that network disappears.

And however many new friendships we build, there is a truth few people like to

admit:

Part of the isolation is inevitable. No matter how sociable you are. No matter

how many friends you make. No matter how much you love the country you live in.

There is a period that lasts months for some people and years for others, in which the

sense of not fully belonging anywhere is part of the journey.

You no longer live the life you left behind. But you also do not yet feel

fully part of the new reality.

It is an emotional no-man’s-land.

And it is precisely in that space that some of the immigrant’s greatest

vulnerabilities begin to appear.

The first of them is projection.

Without noticing, we start expecting new relationships to fill spaces that were

previously occupied by an entire community.

We expect a partner to be best friend, therapist, family and safe harbour all at

the same time.

We expect recent friendships to have the depth of decades.

We expect people we met a few months ago to understand pains built up

over a whole lifetime.

And when that does not happen, the sense of abandonment appears.

But often we are not suffering because of the relationship itself. We are suffering from

the absence of the network that existed before it.

The problem is that there is a second factor that makes all of this even more intense. And it

rarely gets the attention it deserves.

The body. Especially when we talk about physical activity.

Many immigrants, especially those who come from sunny countries, go through

a drastic change of lifestyle.

Less time outdoors. Less exposure to the sun. Less movement. Fewer spontaneous

walks. Fewer in-person meetings. Less human contact.

And without noticing, they enter a dangerous cycle.

They feel more isolated.

They go out less. They move less.

And the less they move, the worse they feel.

What few people know is that movement is not only about losing weight or

improving physical health.

Movement is a tool for emotional regulation.

When we walk, run, train or simply put the body in

movement, we help the nervous system process stress, anxiety, frustration and

sadness.

Physical activity acts as a kind of biological pressure valve.

It reduces stress levels. It improves mood. It promotes sleep. It increases the sense of

energy.

And, perhaps most important for the immigrant, it creates an internal sense of stability.

Because there is something nobody tells us about immigration: not every feeling of

longing is emotional.

Sometimes what we are interpreting as longing is exhaustion. Sometimes what seems like

deep sadness is a lack of sunlight. Sometimes what seems like an existential crisis is a

nervous system that has gone months without releasing accumulated tension.

And no, that does not mean the pain of the distance is not real.

It is.

The longing exists. The losses exist. The missed birthdays exist. The absences

exist.

But when the body is exhausted, sedentary and deprived of natural light, everything becomes bigger.

Rejection seems more painful.

Loneliness seems deeper.

Anxiety seems more intense.

Conflicts seem more serious.

Farewells seem more final.

That is why one of the biggest mistakes an immigrant can make is believing that all of

their emotional challenges will be solved through the mind alone.

Analysis is essential, but it does not nourish the needs of the physical body.

In the vast majority of cases, the only need is for more movement.

More walking. More nature. More fresh air. More contact with the physical world.

Especially during the long winter months.

Because winter does not only affect mood. It affects the perception we have of life.

For someone who grew up surrounded by sun, consecutive months of grey sky can

reduce energy, motivation and the emotional capacity to deal with challenges.

And when we add that to the inevitable isolation of immigration, the effects become even

more evident.

That is why creating a movement routine is not a luxury. It is not vanity. It is not just

a matter of health.

It is an emotional survival strategy.

It is a way of telling the nervous system: “We are far from home, but we are
safe.”

Perhaps the greatest lesson of immigration is realising that belonging is not born only from

the people around us.

It is also born from the relationship we build with ourselves.

And that relationship is not created only through thoughts.

It is created through the small daily choices that help body, mind and

heart walk together.

So the next time you feel the longing is crushing your chest, ask one simple

question before concluding that something is wrong:

Are you really missing home...

Or has it been weeks since your body has been begging to get out of the chair, see the daylight and

remind your nervous system that there is still life happening out there?

With love,

Aria Milioni

dwyer-mcallister-cottage.pt_source: Casa rural restaurada aos pés da montanha Keadeen, palco de um episódio da Rebelião de 1798 e hoje pequeno museu de época.
dwyer-mcallister-cottage.en_description: Restored farmhouse at the foot of Keadeen mountain, scene of an episode of the 1798 Rebellion and today a small period museum.

national-botanic-gardens-kilmacurragh.pt_source: Jardim botânico no condado de Wicklow, parte dos Jardins Botânicos Nacionais, famoso pelos rododendros e pelas árvores raras numa antiga propriedade do século XIX.
national-botanic-gardens-kilmacurragh.pt_title: National Botanic Garden of Ireland – Kilmacurragh
national-botanic-gardens-kilmacurragh.en_description: Botanic garden in County Wicklow, part of the National Botanic Gardens, famous for its rhododendrons and rare trees on a former 19th-century estate.

fore-abbey.pt_source: Ruínas do mosteiro fundado por São Feichin no século VII, num vale tranquilo do condado de Westmeath, com as lendárias “Sete Maravilhas de Fore”.
fore-abbey.en_description: Ruins of the monastery founded by St Feichin in the 7th century, in a tranquil valley in County Westmeath, with the legendary "Seven Wonders of Fore".

roscrea-heritage-centre-roscrea-castle-a.pt_source: Conjunto no centro de Roscrea com um castelo do século XIII, a casa pré-paladiana Damer House e jardins murados com fonte.
roscrea-heritage-centre-roscrea-castle-a.pt_title: Roscrea Castle, Gardens and Damer House/Black Mills
roscrea-heritage-centre-roscrea-castle-a.en_description: A group of buildings in the centre of Roscrea with a 13th-century castle, the pre-Palladian Damer House and walled gardens with a fountain.

the-main-guard.pt_source: Antigo tribunal do século XVII no centro de Clonmel, com arcada de colunas de arenito restaurada e espaço de exposições.
the-main-guard.en_description: A former 17th-century courthouse in the centre of Clonmel, with a restored sandstone columned arcade and an exhibition space.

famine-warhouse-1848.pt_source: Casa de lavoura perto de Ballingarry que foi palco de um cerco sangrento da Rebelião dos Jovens Irlandeses de 1848, hoje museu.
famine-warhouse-1848.en_description: A farmhouse near Ballingarry that was the scene of a bloody siege during the 1848 Young Ireland Rebellion, now a museum.

st-marys-church-gowran.pt_source: Igreja colegiada do final do século XIII, com túmulos medievais dos Butler e esculturas do “Mestre de Gowran”, hoje monumento nacional.
st-marys-church-gowran.en_description: A collegiate church from the late 13th century, with medieval Butler tombs and carvings by the "Gowran Master", now a national monument.

kells-priory.pt_source: O maior recinto eclesiástico murado da Irlanda, fundado por volta de 1193 e conhecido localmente como os “Sete Castelos de Kells”.
kells-priory.en_description: Ireland's largest walled ecclesiastical enclosure, founded around 1193 and known locally as the "Seven Castles of Kells".

dungarvan-castle.pt_source: Castelo anglo-normando de cerca de 1209 que protegia a entrada do porto de Dungarvan, com um raro “shell keep” poligonal.
dungarvan-castle.en_description: An Anglo-Norman castle of about 1209 that guarded the entrance to Dungarvan harbour, with a rare polygonal shell keep.

newmills-corn-and-flax-mills.pt_source: Conjunto industrial do século XIX perto de Letterkenny, com uma das maiores rodas de água em funcionamento do país, que servia a indústria do linho.
newmills-corn-and-flax-mills.en_description: A 19th-century industrial complex near Letterkenny, with one of the largest working waterwheels in the country, which once served the linen industry.

glebe-house-and-gallery.pt_source: Casa regencial de 1828 perto de Letterkenny onde viveu o pintor Derek Hill, com uma coleção de arte que inclui Picasso, Renoir e Braque.
glebe-house-and-gallery.pt_title: Glebe Gallery and Garden – Derek Hill House
glebe-house-and-gallery.en_description: An 1828 Regency house near Letterkenny where the painter Derek Hill lived, with an art collection that includes Picasso, Renoir and Braque.

doe-castle.pt_source: Fortaleza medieval dos séculos XV/XVI à beira-mar em Sheephaven Bay, antiga casa dos chefes MacSweeney; terrenos abertos todo o ano.
doe-castle.en_description: A 15th/16th-century fortress by the sea on Sheephaven Bay, former seat of the MacSweeney chiefs; grounds open all year round.

ballyhack-castle.pt_source: Casa-torre de cerca de 1450 sobre o estuário de Waterford, provavelmente construída pelos Cavaleiros Hospitalários de São João.
ballyhack-castle.en_description: A tower house of around 1450 above the Waterford estuary, probably built by the Knights Hospitallers of St John.

ionad-culturtha-an-phiarsaigh-pearses-co.pt_source: Centro cultural em Ros Muc, no coração da Gaeltacht de Connemara, onde Patrick Pearse construiu a sua casa de verão e que hoje se visita tal como ele a deixou.
ionad-culturtha-an-phiarsaigh-pearses-co.pt_title: Ionad Cultúrtha an Phiarsaigh Conamara- Pearse’s Cottage and Visitor Centre
ionad-culturtha-an-phiarsaigh-pearses-co.en_description: A cultural centre in Ros Muc, in the heart of the Connemara Gaeltacht, where Patrick Pearse built his summer house, visited today just as he left it.

aughnanure-castle.pt_source: Casa-torre tardo-medieval mais bem preservada de Connemara, sobre um afloramento rochoso do rio Drimneen, perto do Lough Corrib.
aughnanure-castle.en_description: The best-preserved late-medieval tower house in Connemara, on a rocky outcrop on the River Drimneen, near Lough Corrib.

athenry-castle.pt_source: Casa-torre do século XIII que guardava um vau estratégico no rio Clareen, no centro de uma das vilas medievais mais bem preservadas da Irlanda.
athenry-castle.en_description: A 13th-century tower house that guarded a strategic ford on the River Clareen, in the centre of one of Ireland's best-preserved medieval towns.

desmond-castle-newcastlewest.pt_source: Salão de banquetes medieval do século XV no centro de Newcastle West, com galeria de carvalho restaurada; acesso por visita guiada.
desmond-castle-newcastlewest.en_description: A 15th-century medieval banqueting hall in the centre of Newcastle West, with a restored oak gallery; access by guided tour.

desmond-castle-adare.pt_source: Castelo medieval fortificado nas margens do rio Maigue, com torre quadrada e fosso, ligado aos condes de Desmond; acesso pelo Adare Heritage Centre.
desmond-castle-adare.en_description: A fortified medieval castle on the banks of the River Maigue, with a square tower and moat, linked to the Earls of Desmond; access via the Adare Heritage Centre.

askeaton-castle.pt_source: Ruínas de uma fortaleza medieval de 1199 no centro de Askeaton, antiga base dos condes de Desmond — atualmente fechada, apenas vista exterior.
askeaton-castle.en_description: Ruins of a medieval fortress of 1199 in the centre of Askeaton, former base of the Earls of Desmond — currently closed, exterior viewing only.

blasket-centre-ionad-an-bhlascaoid.pt_source: Centro de património dedicado à comunidade de língua irlandesa das Ilhas Blasket, com exposições interativas e miradouro sobre o Atlântico.
blasket-centre-ionad-an-bhlascaoid.pt_title: Ionad an Bhlascaoid – The Blasket Centre
blasket-centre-ionad-an-bhlascaoid.en_description: A heritage centre dedicated to the Irish-speaking community of the Blasket Islands, with interactive exhibitions and a viewpoint over the Atlantic.

listowel-castle.pt_source: Castelo anglo-normando sobre o rio Feale, último reduto dos Fitzmaurice na Guerra dos Nove Anos, com acesso por visita guiada.
listowel-castle.en_description: An Anglo-Norman castle above the River Feale, the Fitzmaurices' last stronghold in the Nine Years' War, with access by guided tour.

ardfert-cathedral.pt_source: Conjunto de três igrejas medievais, a mais antiga do século XII, no local do mosteiro fundado por São Brandão, o Navegador.
ardfert-cathedral.en_description: A group of three medieval churches, the oldest from the 12th century, on the site of the monastery founded by St Brendan the Navigator.

aras-an-uachtarain.en_description: The official residence of the President of Ireland, in Phoenix Park, with free guided tours on Saturdays, subject to State business.

st-stephens-green.en_description: One of Ireland's best-known public parks, in the heart of Dublin's shopping district, kept to its original Victorian layout.

st-audens-church.en_description: Dublin's only surviving medieval parish church, dedicated to the bishop of Rouen, with the St Anne's Guild Chapel and the Portlester tomb.

st-marys-abbey-chapter-house.pt_source: Restos de um dos maiores e mais importantes mosteiros medievais da Irlanda, com acesso apenas por visita guiada e abertura sazonal.
st-marys-abbey-chapter-house.pt_title: St. Mary’s Abbey – Chapter House – Cistercian Monastery
st-marys-abbey-chapter-house.en_description: Remains of one of the largest and most important medieval monasteries in Ireland, accessible by guided tour only and open seasonally.

royal-hospital-kilmainham.pt_source: Um dos edifícios mais emblemáticos de Dublin e o melhor exemplo irlandês de arquitetura do século XVII, hoje sede do Museu Irlandês de Arte Moderna.
royal-hospital-kilmainham.en_description: One of Dublin's most landmark buildings and Ireland's finest example of 17th-century architecture, today home to the Irish Museum of Modern Art.

rathfarnham-castle.pt_source: Castelo isabelino do século XVI com quatro torres, remodelado no século XVIII, com retratos de família e exposições culturais.
rathfarnham-castle.en_description: A 16th-century Elizabethan castle with four towers, remodelled in the 18th century, with family portraits and cultural exhibitions.
